בְּנֵ֣י שִׁמְעִ֗י (שלמות) [שְׁלֹמִ֧ית] וַחֲזִיאֵ֛ל וְהָרָ֖ן שְׁלֹשָׁ֑ה אֵ֛לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֥י הָאָב֖וֹת לְלַעְדָּֽן׃ ס
וּבְנֵ֣י שִׁמְעִ֔י יַ֣חַת זִינָ֔א וִיע֖וּשׁ וּבְרִיעָ֑ה אֵ֥לֶּה בְנֵֽי־שִׁמְעִ֖י אַרְבָּעָֽה׃
וַיְהִי־יַ֣חַת הָרֹ֔אשׁ וְזִיזָ֖ה הַשֵּׁנִ֑י וִיע֤וּשׁ וּבְרִיעָה֙ לֹא־הִרְבּ֣וּ בָנִ֔ים וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ לְבֵ֣ית אָ֔ב לִפְקֻדָּ֖ה אֶחָֽת׃ ס
בְּנֵ֣י קְהָ֗ת עַמְרָ֥ם יִצְהָ֛ר חֶבְר֥וֹן וְעֻזִּיאֵ֖ל אַרְבָּעָֽה׃ ס
בְּנֵ֥י עַמְרָ֖ם אַהֲרֹ֣ן וּמֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּבָּדֵ֣ל אַהֲרֹ֡ן לְֽהַקְדִּישׁוֹ֩ קֹ֨דֶשׁ קׇדָשִׁ֤ים הֽוּא־וּבָנָיו֙ עַד־עוֹלָ֔ם לְהַקְטִיר֩ לִפְנֵ֨י יְהֹוָ֧ה לְשָׁרְת֛וֹ וּלְבָרֵ֥ךְ בִּשְׁמ֖וֹ עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
וּמֹשֶׁ֖ה אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים בָּנָ֕יו יִקָּרְא֖וּ עַל־שֵׁ֥בֶט הַלֵּוִֽי׃ ס
בְּנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה גֵּרְשׁ֖וֹם וֶאֱלִיעֶֽזֶר׃
בְּנֵ֥י גֵרְשׁ֖וֹם שְׁבוּאֵ֥ל הָרֹֽאשׁ׃
וַיִּהְי֥וּ בְנֵֽי־אֱלִיעֶ֖זֶר רְחַבְיָ֣ה הָרֹ֑אשׁ וְלֹא־הָיָ֤ה לֶאֱלִיעֶ֙זֶר֙ בָּנִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וּבְנֵ֥י רְחַבְיָ֖ה רָב֥וּ לְמָֽעְלָה׃ ס
בְּנֵ֥י יִצְהָ֖ר שְׁלֹמִ֥ית הָרֹֽאשׁ׃
בְּנֵ֖י חֶבְר֑וֹן יְרִיָּ֤הוּ הָרֹאשׁ֙ אֲמַרְיָ֣ה הַשֵּׁנִ֔י יַֽחֲזִיאֵל֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י וִֽיקַמְעָ֖ם הָרְבִיעִֽי׃
בְּנֵ֖י עֻזִּיאֵ֑ל מִיכָ֣ה הָרֹ֔אשׁ וְיִשִּׁיָּ֖ה הַשֵּׁנִֽי׃
בְּנֵ֤י מְרָרִי֙ מַחְלִ֣י וּמוּשִׁ֔י בְּנֵ֥י מַחְלִ֖י אֶלְעָזָ֥ר וְקִֽישׁ׃
וַיָּ֙מׇת֙ אֶלְעָזָ֔ר וְלֹא־הָ֥יוּ ל֛וֹ בָּנִ֖ים כִּ֣י אִם־בָּנ֑וֹת וַיִּשָּׂא֥וּם בְּנֵי־קִ֖ישׁ אֲחֵיהֶֽם׃
בְּנֵ֣י מוּשִׁ֗י מַחְלִ֥י וְעֵ֛דֶר וִירֵמ֖וֹת שְׁלוֹשָֽׁה׃ ס

אֵ֣לֶּה בְנֵֽי־לֵוִי֩ לְבֵ֨ית אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֜ם רָאשֵׁ֧י הָאָב֣וֹת לִפְקוּדֵיהֶ֗ם בְּמִסְפַּ֤ר שֵׁמוֹת֙ לְגֻלְגְּלֹתָ֔ם עֹשֵׂה֙ הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה לַעֲבֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֣ית יְהֹוָ֑ה מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָֽעְלָה׃
כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר דָּוִ֔יד הֵנִ֛יחַ יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְעַמּ֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁכֹּ֥ן בִּירוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם עַד־לְעוֹלָֽם׃
וְגַ֖ם לַלְוִיִּ֑ם אֵין־לָשֵׂ֧את אֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן וְאֶת־כׇּל־כֵּלָ֖יו לַעֲבֹדָתֽוֹ׃
כִּ֣י בְדִבְרֵ֤י דָוִיד֙ הָאַ֣חֲרוֹנִ֔ים הֵ֖מָּה מִסְפַּ֣ר בְּנֵֽי־לֵוִ֑י מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּלְמָֽעְלָה׃
כִּ֣י מַעֲמָדָ֞ם לְיַד־בְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֗ן לַֽעֲבֹדַת֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהֹוָ֔ה עַל־הַֽחֲצֵרוֹת֙ וְעַל־הַלְּשָׁכ֔וֹת וְעַֽל־טׇהֳרַ֖ת לְכׇל־קֹ֑דֶשׁ וּמַֽעֲשֵׂ֔ה עֲבֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
וּלְלֶ֨חֶם הַֽמַּעֲרֶ֜כֶת וּלְסֹ֤לֶת לְמִנְחָה֙ וְלִרְקִיקֵ֣י הַמַּצּ֔וֹת וְלַֽמַּחֲבַ֖ת וְלַמֻּרְבָּ֑כֶת וּלְכׇל־מְשׂוּרָ֖ה וּמִדָּֽה׃
וְלַֽעֲמֹד֙ בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֔קֶר לְהֹד֥וֹת וּלְהַלֵּ֖ל לַֽיהֹוָ֑ה וְכֵ֖ן לָעָֽרֶב׃
וּלְכֹ֨ל הַעֲל֤וֹת עֹלוֹת֙ לַֽיהֹוָ֔ה לַשַּׁ֨בָּת֔וֹת לֶחֳדָשִׁ֖ים וְלַמֹּעֲדִ֑ים בְּמִסְפָּ֨ר כְּמִשְׁפָּ֧ט עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם תָּמִ֖יד לִפְנֵ֥י יְהֹוָֽה׃
וְשָׁמְר֞וּ אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת אֹֽהֶל־מוֹעֵ֗ד וְאֵת֙ מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ וּמִשְׁמֶ֕רֶת בְּנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹ֖ן אֲחֵיהֶ֑ם לַעֲבֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֥ית יְהֹוָֽה׃ פ
וְלִבְנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹ֖ן מַחְלְקוֹתָ֑ם בְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֔ן נָדָב֙ וַאֲבִיה֔וּא אֶלְעָזָ֖ר וְאִיתָמָֽר׃
וַיָּ֨מׇת נָדָ֤ב וַֽאֲבִיהוּא֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אֲבִיהֶ֔ם וּבָנִ֖ים לֹא־הָי֣וּ לָהֶ֑ם וַֽיְכַהֲנ֔וּ אֶלְעָזָ֖ר וְאִיתָמָֽר׃
וַיֶּחָלְקֵ֣ם דָּוִ֔יד וְצָדוֹק֙ מִן־בְּנֵ֣י אֶלְעָזָ֔ר וַאֲחִימֶ֖לֶךְ מִן־בְּנֵ֣י אִיתָמָ֑ר לִפְקֻדָּתָ֖ם בַּעֲבֹדָתָֽם׃

וַיִּמָּצְא֣וּ בְֽנֵי־אֶלְעָזָ֡ר רַבִּ֞ים לְרָאשֵׁ֧י הַגְּבָרִ֛ים מִן־בְּנֵ֥י אִיתָמָ֖ר וַֽיַּחְלְק֑וּם לִבְנֵ֨י אֶלְעָזָ֜ר רָאשִׁ֤ים לְבֵית־אָבוֹת֙ שִׁשָּׁ֣ה עָשָׂ֔ר וְלִבְנֵ֧י אִיתָמָ֛ר לְבֵ֥ית אֲבוֹתָ֖ם שְׁמוֹנָֽה׃
וַיַּחְלְק֥וּם בְּגוֹרָל֖וֹת אֵ֣לֶּה עִם־אֵ֑לֶּה כִּֽי־הָי֤וּ שָׂרֵי־קֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים מִבְּנֵ֥י אֶלְעָזָ֖ר וּבִבְנֵ֥י אִיתָמָֽר׃ ס

וַֽיִּכְתְּבֵ֡ם שְֽׁמַעְיָה֩ בֶן־נְתַנְאֵ֨ל הַסּוֹפֵ֜ר מִן־הַלֵּוִ֗י לִפְנֵ֨י הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ וְהַשָּׂרִים֙ וְצָד֣וֹק הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וַאֲחִימֶ֙לֶךְ֙ בֶּן־אֶבְיָתָ֔ר וְרָאשֵׁי֙ הָאָב֔וֹת לַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְלַלְוִיִּ֑ם בֵּֽית־אָ֣ב אֶחָ֗ד אָחֻז֙ לְאֶלְעָזָ֔ר וְאָחֻ֥ז ׀ אָחֻ֖ז לְאִיתָמָֽר׃ פ
וַיֵּצֵ֞א הַגּוֹרָ֤ל הָֽרִאשׁוֹן֙ לִיה֣וֹיָרִ֔יב {ס}        לִידַֽעְיָ֖ה הַשֵּׁנִֽי׃ ס
לְחָרִם֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י {ס}        לִשְׂעֹרִ֖ים הָרְבִעִֽי׃ ס
לְמַלְכִּיָּה֙ הַחֲמִישִׁ֔י {ס}        לְמִיָּמִ֖ן הַשִּׁשִּֽׁי׃ ס
לְהַקּוֹץ֙ הַשְּׁבִעִ֔י {ס}        לַאֲבִיָּ֖ה הַשְּׁמִינִֽי׃ ס
לְיֵשׁ֙וּעַ֙ הַתְּשִׁעִ֔י {ס}        לִשְׁכַנְיָ֖הוּ הָעֲשִׂרִֽי׃ ס
לְאֶלְיָשִׁיב֙ עַשְׁתֵּ֣י עָשָׂ֔ר {ס}        לְיָקִ֖ים שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
לְחֻפָּה֙ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה עָשָׂ֔ר {ס}        לְיֶשֶׁבְאָ֖ב אַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
לְבִלְגָּה֙ חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה עָשָׂ֔ר {ס}        לְאִמֵּ֖ר שִׁשָּׁ֥ה עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
לְחֵזִיר֙ שִׁבְעָ֣ה עָשָׂ֔ר {ס}        לְהַפִּצֵּ֖ץ שְׁמוֹנָ֥ה עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
לִֽפְתַחְיָה֙ תִּשְׁעָ֣ה עָשָׂ֔ר {ס}        לִֽיחֶזְקֵ֖אל הָעֶשְׂרִֽים׃ ס
לְיָכִין֙ אֶחָ֣ד וְעֶשְׂרִ֔ים {ס}        לְגָמ֖וּל שְׁנַ֥יִם וְעֶשְׂרִֽים׃ ס
לִדְלָיָ֙הוּ֙ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֔ים {ס}        לְמַעַזְיָ֖הוּ אַרְבָּעָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִֽים׃ פ
אֵ֣לֶּה פְקֻדָּתָ֞ם לַעֲבֹדָתָ֗ם לָב֤וֹא לְבֵית־יְהֹוָה֙ כְּמִשְׁפָּטָ֔ם בְּיַ֖ד אַהֲרֹ֣ן אֲבִיהֶ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֔הוּ יְהֹוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ פ
וְלִבְנֵ֥י לֵוִ֖י הַנּוֹתָרִ֑ים לִבְנֵ֤י עַמְרָם֙ שֽׁוּבָאֵ֔ל לִבְנֵ֥י שׁוּבָאֵ֖ל יֶחְדְּיָֽהוּ׃ ס
לִרְחַבְיָ֑הוּ לִבְנֵ֣י רְחַבְיָ֔הוּ הָרֹ֖אשׁ יִשִּׁיָּֽה׃ ס
לַיִּצְהָרִ֣י שְׁלֹמ֔וֹת לִבְנֵ֥י שְׁלֹמ֖וֹת יָֽחַת׃ ס
וּבְנָ֖י יְרִיָּ֑הוּ אֲמַרְיָ֙הוּ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י יַחֲזִיאֵל֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י יְקַמְעָ֖ם הָרְבִיעִֽי׃ ס
בְּנֵ֤י עֻזִּיאֵל֙ מִיכָ֔ה לִבְנֵ֥י מִיכָ֖ה (שמור) [שָׁמִֽיר]׃
אֲחִ֤י מִיכָה֙ יִשִּׁיָּ֔ה {ס}        לִבְנֵ֥י יִשִּׁיָּ֖ה זְכַרְיָֽהוּ׃ ס
בְּנֵ֤י מְרָרִי֙ מַחְלִ֣י וּמוּשִׁ֔י {ס}        בְּנֵ֖י יַעֲזִיָּ֥הוּ בְנֽוֹ׃ ס
בְּנֵ֖י מְרָרִ֑י לְיַעֲזִיָּ֣הוּ בְנ֔וֹ וְשֹׁ֥הַם וְזַכּ֖וּר וְעִבְרִֽי׃ ס
לְמַחְלִי֙ אֶלְעָזָ֔ר וְלֹא־הָ֥יָה ל֖וֹ בָּנִֽים׃ ס
לְקִ֖ישׁ בְּנֵי־קִ֥ישׁ יְרַחְמְאֵֽל׃ ס
וּבְנֵ֣י מוּשִׁ֔י מַחְלִ֥י וְעֵ֖דֶר וִירִימ֑וֹת אֵ֛לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י הַלְוִיִּ֖ם לְבֵ֥ית אֲבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

וַיַּפִּ֩ילוּ֩ גַם־הֵ֨ם גּוֹרָל֜וֹת לְעֻמַּ֣ת ׀ אֲחֵיהֶ֣ם בְּנֵי־אַהֲרֹ֗ן לִפְנֵ֨י דָוִ֤יד הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וְצָד֣וֹק וַאֲחִימֶ֔לֶךְ וְרָאשֵׁי֙ הָאָב֔וֹת לַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְלַלְוִיִּ֑ם אָב֣וֹת הָרֹ֔אשׁ לְעֻמַּ֖ת אָחִ֥יו הַקָּטָֽן׃ ס

וַיַּבְדֵּ֣ל דָּוִיד֩ וְשָׂרֵ֨י הַצָּבָ֜א לַעֲבֹדָ֗ה לִבְנֵ֤י אָסָף֙ וְהֵימָ֣ן וִידוּת֔וּן (הנביאים) [הַֽנִּבְּאִ֛ים] בְּכִנֹּר֥וֹת בִּנְבָלִ֖ים וּבִמְצִלְתָּ֑יִם וַֽיְהִי֙ מִסְפָּרָ֔ם אַנְשֵׁ֥י מְלָאכָ֖ה לַעֲבֹדָתָֽם׃
לִבְנֵ֣י אָסָ֗ף זַכּ֧וּר וְיוֹסֵ֛ף וּנְתַנְיָ֥ה וַאֲשַׂרְאֵ֖לָה בְּנֵ֣י אָסָ֑ף עַ֚ל יַד־אָסָ֔ף הַנִּבָּ֖א עַל־יְדֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

לִידוּת֑וּן בְּנֵ֣י יְדוּת֡וּן גְּדַלְיָ֡הוּ וּצְרִ֡י וִ֠ישַׁעְיָ֠הוּ חֲשַׁבְיָ֨הוּ וּמַתִּתְיָ֜הוּ שִׁשָּׁ֗ה עַל֩ יְדֵ֨י אֲבִיהֶ֤ם יְדוּתוּן֙ בַּכִּנּ֔וֹר הַנִּבָּ֕א עַל־הֹד֥וֹת וְהַלֵּ֖ל לַיהֹוָֽה׃ ס

לְהֵימָ֑ן בְּנֵ֣י הֵימָ֡ן בֻּקִּיָּ֡הוּ מַתַּנְיָ֡הוּ עֻ֠זִּיאֵ֠ל שְׁבוּאֵ֨ל וִירִימ֜וֹת חֲנַנְיָ֣ה חֲנָ֗נִי אֱלִיאָ֤תָה גִדַּ֙לְתִּי֙ וְרֹמַ֣מְתִּי עֶ֔זֶר יׇשְׁבְּקָ֣שָׁה מַלּ֔וֹתִי הוֹתִ֖יר מַחֲזִיאֹֽת׃
כׇּל־אֵ֨לֶּה בָנִ֜ים לְהֵימָ֗ן חֹזֵ֥ה הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ בְּדִבְרֵ֥י הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים לְהָרִ֣ים קָ֑רֶן וַיִּתֵּ֨ן הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים לְהֵימָ֗ן בָּנִ֛ים אַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר וּבָנ֥וֹת שָׁלֽוֹשׁ׃
כׇּל־אֵ֣לֶּה עַל־יְדֵי֩ אֲבִיהֶ֨ם בַּשִּׁ֜יר בֵּ֣ית יְהֹוָ֗ה בִּמְצִלְתַּ֙יִם֙ נְבָלִ֣ים וְכִנֹּר֔וֹת לַעֲבֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים עַ֚ל יְדֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אָסָ֥ף וִידוּת֖וּן וְהֵימָֽן׃
וַיְהִ֤י מִסְפָּרָם֙ עִם־אֲחֵיהֶ֔ם מְלֻמְּדֵי־שִׁ֖יר לַיהֹוָ֑ה כׇּ֨ל־הַמֵּבִ֔ין מָאתַ֖יִם שְׁמוֹנִ֥ים וּשְׁמוֹנָֽה׃
וַיַּפִּ֜ילוּ גּוֹרָל֣וֹת מִשְׁמֶ֗רֶת לְעֻמַּת֙ כַּקָּטֹ֣ן כַּגָּד֔וֹל מֵבִ֖ין עִם־תַּלְמִֽיד׃ פ
וַיֵּצֵ֞א הַגּוֹרָ֧ל הָרִאשׁ֛וֹן לְאָסָ֖ף לְיוֹסֵ֑ף {ס}        גְּדַלְיָ֙הוּ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י הֽוּא־וְאֶחָ֥יו וּבָנָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֣י זַכּ֔וּר בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
הָֽרְבִיעִי֙ לַיִּצְרִ֔י בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
הַחֲמִישִׁ֣י נְתַנְיָ֔הוּ בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
הַשִּׁשִּׁ֣י בֻקִּיָּ֔הוּ בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
הַשְּׁבִעִ֣י יְשַׂרְאֵ֔לָה בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
הַשְּׁמִינִ֣י יְשַֽׁעְיָ֔הוּ בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
הַתְּשִׁיעִ֣י מַתַּנְיָ֔הוּ בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
הָעֲשִׂירִ֣י שִׁמְעִ֔י בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
עַשְׁתֵּי־עָשָׂ֣ר עֲזַרְאֵ֔ל בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
הַשְּׁנֵ֤ים עָשָׂר֙ לַֽחֲשַׁבְיָ֔ה בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
לִשְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ שֽׁוּבָאֵ֔ל בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
לְאַרְבָּעָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ מַתִּתְיָ֔הוּ בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
לַחֲמִשָּׁ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ לִירֵמ֔וֹת בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
לְשִׁשָּׁ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ לַחֲנַנְיָ֔הוּ בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
לְשִׁבְעָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ לְיׇשְׁבְּקָ֔שָׁה בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
לִשְׁמוֹנָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ לַחֲנָ֔נִי בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
לְתִשְׁעָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ לְמַלּ֔וֹתִי בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
לְעֶשְׂרִים֙ לֶאֱלִיָּ֔תָה בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
לְאֶחָ֤ד וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ לְהוֹתִ֔יר בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
לִשְׁנַ֤יִם וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ לְגִדַּ֔לְתִּי בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
לִשְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ לְמַ֣חֲזִיא֔וֹת בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
לְאַרְבָּעָ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ לְרוֹמַ֣מְתִּי עָ֔זֶר בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶחָ֖יו שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃ פ
לְמַחְלְק֖וֹת לְשֹׁעֲרִ֑ים לַקׇּרְחִ֕ים מְשֶׁלֶמְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־קֹרֵ֖א מִן־בְּנֵ֥י אָסָֽף׃
וְלִמְשֶׁלֶמְיָ֖הוּ בָּנִ֑ים זְכַרְיָ֤הוּ הַבְּכוֹר֙ יְדִיעֲאֵ֣ל הַשֵּׁנִ֔י זְבַדְיָ֙הוּ֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י יַתְנִיאֵ֖ל הָרְבִיעִֽי׃
עֵילָ֤ם הַחֲמִישִׁי֙ יְהוֹחָנָ֣ן הַשִּׁשִּׁ֔י אֶלְיְהוֹעֵינַ֖י הַשְּׁבִיעִֽי׃
וּלְעֹבֵ֥ד אֱדֹ֖ם בָּנִ֑ים שְׁמַעְיָ֤ה הַבְּכוֹר֙ יְהוֹזָבָ֣ד הַשֵּׁנִ֔י יוֹאָ֤ח הַשְּׁלִשִׁי֙ וְשָׂכָ֣ר הָרְבִיעִ֔י וּנְתַנְאֵ֖ל הַחֲמִישִֽׁי׃
עַמִּיאֵ֤ל הַשִּׁשִּׁי֙ יִשָּׂשכָ֣ר הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י פְּעֻלְּתַ֖י הַשְּׁמִינִ֑י כִּ֥י בֵרְכ֖וֹ אֱלֹהִֽים׃ ס
וְלִֽשְׁמַעְיָ֤ה בְנוֹ֙ נוֹלַ֣ד בָּנִ֔ים הַמִּמְשָׁלִ֖ים לְבֵ֣ית אֲבִיהֶ֑ם כִּֽי־גִבּ֥וֹרֵי חַ֖יִל הֵֽמָּה׃
בְּנֵ֣י שְׁמַֽעְיָ֗ה עׇ֠תְנִ֠י וּרְפָאֵ֨ל וְעוֹבֵ֧ד אֶלְזָבָ֛ד אֶחָ֖יו בְּנֵי־חָ֑יִל אֱלִיה֖וּ וּסְמַכְיָֽהוּ׃
כׇּל־אֵ֜לֶּה מִבְּנֵ֣י ׀ עֹבֵ֣ד אֱדֹ֗ם הֵ֤מָּה וּבְנֵיהֶם֙ וַאֲחֵיהֶ֔ם אִֽישׁ־חַ֥יִל בַּכֹּ֖חַ לַעֲבֹדָ֑ה שִׁשִּׁ֥ים וּשְׁנַ֖יִם לְעֹבֵ֥ד אֱדֹֽם׃
וְלִמְשֶׁלֶמְיָ֗הוּ בָּנִ֧ים וְאַחִ֛ים בְּנֵי־חָ֖יִל שְׁמוֹנָ֥ה עָשָֽׂר׃ ס
וּלְחֹסָ֥ה מִן־בְּנֵי־מְרָרִ֖י בָּנִ֑ים שִׁמְרִ֤י הָרֹאשׁ֙ כִּ֣י לֹֽא־הָיָ֣ה בְכ֔וֹר וַיְשִׂימֵ֥הוּ אָבִ֖יהוּ לְרֹֽאשׁ׃
חִלְקִיָּ֤הוּ הַשֵּׁנִי֙ טְבַלְיָ֣הוּ הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֔י זְכַרְיָ֖הוּ הָרְבִעִ֑י כׇּל־בָּנִ֧ים וְאַחִ֛ים לְחֹסָ֖ה שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה עָשָֽׂר׃
לְ֠אֵ֠לֶּה מַחְלְק֨וֹת הַשֹּׁעֲרִ֜ים לְרָאשֵׁ֧י הַגְּבָרִ֛ים מִשְׁמָר֖וֹת לְעֻמַּ֣ת אֲחֵיהֶ֑ם לְשָׁרֵ֖ת בְּבֵ֥ית יְהֹוָֽה׃
וַיַּפִּ֨ילוּ גוֹרָל֜וֹת כַּקָּטֹ֧ן כַּגָּד֛וֹל לְבֵ֥ית אֲבוֹתָ֖ם לְשַׁ֥עַר וָשָֽׁעַר׃ פ
וַיִּפֹּ֧ל הַגּוֹרָ֛ל מִזְרָ֖חָה לְשֶׁלֶמְיָ֑הוּ וּזְכַרְיָ֨הוּ בְנ֜וֹ יוֹעֵ֣ץ ׀ בְּשֶׂ֗כֶל הִפִּ֙ילוּ֙ גּֽוֹרָל֔וֹת וַיֵּצֵ֥א גוֹרָל֖וֹ צָפֽוֹנָה׃
לְעֹבֵ֥ד אֱדֹ֖ם נֶ֑גְבָּה וּלְבָנָ֖יו בֵּ֥ית הָאֲסֻפִּֽים׃
לְשֻׁפִּ֤ים וּלְחֹסָה֙ לַֽמַּעֲרָ֔ב עִ֚ם שַׁ֣עַר שַׁלֶּ֔כֶת בַּֽמְסִלָּ֖ה הָעוֹלָ֑ה מִשְׁמָ֖ר לְעֻמַּ֥ת מִשְׁמָֽר׃ ס
לַמִּזְרָח֮ הַלְוִיִּ֣ם שִׁשָּׁה֒ לַצָּפ֤וֹנָה לַיּוֹם֙ אַרְבָּעָ֔ה לַנֶּ֥גְבָּה לַיּ֖וֹם אַרְבָּעָ֑ה {ס}        וְלָאֲסֻפִּ֖ים שְׁנַ֥יִם שְׁנָֽיִם׃
לַפַּרְבָּ֖ר לַֽמַּעֲרָ֑ב אַרְבָּעָה֙ לַֽמְסִלָּ֔ה שְׁנַ֖יִם לַפַּרְבָּֽר׃
אֵ֗לֶּה מַחְלְקוֹת֙ הַשֹּׁ֣עֲרִ֔ים לִבְנֵ֥י הַקׇּרְחִ֖י וְלִבְנֵ֥י מְרָרִֽי׃
וְֽהַלְוִיִּ֑ם אֲחִיָּ֗ה עַל־אֽוֹצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּלְאֹצְר֖וֹת הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים׃ ס
בְּנֵ֣י לַ֠עְדָּ֠ן בְּנֵ֨י הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֜י לְלַעְדָּ֗ן רָאשֵׁ֧י הָאָב֛וֹת לְלַעְדָּ֥ן הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּ֖י יְחִיאֵלִֽי׃ ס
בְּנֵ֖י יְחִיאֵלִ֑י זֵתָם֙ וְיוֹאֵ֣ל אָחִ֔יו עַל־אֹצְר֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית יְהֹוָֽה׃ ס
לַֽעַמְרָמִי֙ לַיִּצְהָרִ֔י לַחֶבְרוֹנִ֖י לָעׇזִּיאֵלִֽי׃
וּשְׁבֻאֵל֙ בֶּן־גֵּרְשׁ֣וֹם בֶּן־מֹשֶׁ֔ה נָגִ֖יד עַל־הָאֹצָרֽוֹת׃ ס
וְאֶחָ֖יו לֶאֱלִיעֶ֑זֶר רְחַבְיָ֨הוּ בְנ֜וֹ וִישַׁעְיָ֤הֽוּ בְנוֹ֙ וְיֹרָ֣ם בְּנ֔וֹ וְזִכְרִ֥י בְנ֖וֹ (ושלמות) [וּשְׁלֹמִ֥ית] בְּנֽוֹ׃
ה֧וּא שְׁלֹמ֣וֹת וְאֶחָ֗יו עַ֣ל כׇּל־אֹצְר֤וֹת הַקֳּדָשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִקְדִּ֜ישׁ דָּוִ֣יד הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וְרָאשֵׁ֧י הָאָב֛וֹת לְשָׂרֵֽי־הָאֲלָפִ֥ים וְהַמֵּא֖וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֥י הַצָּבָֽא׃
מִן־הַמִּלְחָמ֥וֹת וּמִן־הַשָּׁלָ֖ל הִקְדִּ֑ישׁוּ לְחַזֵּ֖ק לְבֵ֥ית יְהֹוָֽה׃
וְכֹ֨ל הַהִקְדִּ֜ישׁ שְׁמוּאֵ֤ל הָרֹאֶה֙ וְשָׁא֣וּל בֶּן־קִ֔ישׁ וְאַבְנֵ֣ר בֶּן־נֵ֔ר וְיוֹאָ֖ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֑ה כֹּ֚ל הַמַּקְדִּ֔ישׁ עַ֥ל יַד־שְׁלֹמִ֖ית וְאֶחָֽיו׃ פ
לַיִּצְהָרִ֞י כְּנַנְיָ֣הוּ וּבָנָ֗יו לַמְּלָאכָ֤ה הַחִֽיצוֹנָה֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְשֹׁטְרִ֖ים וּלְשֹׁפְטִֽים׃
לַחֶבְרוֹנִ֡י חֲשַׁבְיָ֩הוּ֩ וְאֶחָ֨יו בְּנֵי־חַ֜יִל אֶ֣לֶף וּשְׁבַע־מֵא֗וֹת עַ֚ל פְּקֻדַּ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מֵעֵ֥בֶר לַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן מַעְרָ֑בָה לְכֹל֙ מְלֶ֣אכֶת יְהֹוָ֔ה וְלַעֲבֹדַ֖ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִי֙ יְרִיָּ֣ה הָרֹ֔אשׁ לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִ֥י לְתֹלְדֹתָ֖יו לְאָב֑וֹת בִּשְׁנַ֨ת הָאַרְבָּעִ֜ים לְמַלְכ֤וּת דָּוִיד֙ נִדְרָ֔שׁוּ וַיִּמָּצֵ֥א בָהֶ֛ם גִּבּ֥וֹרֵי חַ֖יִל בְּיַעְזֵ֥יר גִּלְעָֽד׃

וְאֶחָ֣יו בְּנֵי־חַ֗יִל אַלְפַּ֛יִם וּשְׁבַ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֑וֹת וַֽיַּפְקִידֵ֞ם דָּוִ֣יד הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עַל־הָראוּבֵנִ֤י וְהַגָּדִי֙ וַחֲצִי֙ שֵׁ֣בֶט הַֽמְנַשִּׁ֔י לְכׇל־דְּבַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים וּדְבַ֥ר הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ פ

וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל ׀ לְֽמִסְפָּרָ֡ם רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֣וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָאֲלָפִ֣ים ׀ וְהַמֵּא֡וֹת וְשֹׁטְרֵיהֶם֩ הַמְשָׁרְתִ֨ים אֶת־הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְכֹ֣ל ׀ דְּבַ֣ר הַֽמַּחְלְק֗וֹת הַבָּאָ֤ה וְהַיֹּצֵאת֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ בְּחֹ֔דֶשׁ לְכֹ֖ל חׇדְשֵׁ֣י הַשָּׁנָ֑ה הַֽמַּחֲלֹ֙קֶת֙ הָאַחַ֔ת עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ פ
עַ֞ל הַמַּחֲלֹ֤קֶת הָרִֽאשׁוֹנָה֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן יָשׇׁבְעָ֖ם בֶּן־זַבְדִּיאֵ֑ל וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ ס
מִן־בְּנֵי־פֶ֗רֶץ הָרֹ֛אשׁ לְכׇל־שָׂרֵ֥י הַצְּבָא֖וֹת לַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָרִאשֽׁוֹן׃ ס
וְעַ֞ל מַחֲלֹ֣קֶת ׀ הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֗י דּוֹדַ֤י הָֽאֲחוֹחִי֙ וּמַ֣חֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ וּמִקְל֖וֹת הַנָּגִ֑יד וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ ס
שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֤א הַשְּׁלִישִׁי֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י בְּנָיָ֧הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֛ע הַכֹּהֵ֖ן רֹ֑אשׁ וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃
ה֧וּא בְנָיָ֛הוּ גִּבּ֥וֹר הַשְּׁלֹשִׁ֖ים וְעַל־הַשְּׁלֹשִׁ֑ים וּמַ֣חֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עַמִּיזָבָ֖ד בְּנֽוֹ׃ ס
הָרְבִיעִ֞י לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרְבִיעִ֗י עֲשָׂהאֵל֙ אֲחִ֣י יוֹאָ֔ב וּזְבַדְיָ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ אַחֲרָ֑יו וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ ס
הַחֲמִישִׁי֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַחֲמִישִׁ֔י הַשַּׂ֖ר שַׁמְה֣וּת הַיִּזְרָ֑ח וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ ס
הַשִּׁשִּׁי֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשִּׁשִּׁ֔י עִירָ֥א בֶן־עִקֵּ֖שׁ הַתְּקוֹעִ֑י וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ ס
הַשְּׁבִיעִי֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י חֶ֥לֶץ הַפְּלוֹנִ֖י מִן־בְּנֵ֣י אֶפְרָ֑יִם וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ ס
הַשְּׁמִינִי֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁמִינִ֔י סִבְּכַ֥י הַחֻשָׁתִ֖י לַזַּרְחִ֑י וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ ס
הַתְּשִׁיעִי֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַתְּשִׁיעִ֔י אֲבִיעֶ֥זֶר הָעַנְּתוֹתִ֖י (לבנימיני) [לַבֵּ֣ן ׀ יְמִינִ֑י] וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ ס
הָעֲשִׂירִי֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִ֔י מַהְרַ֥י הַנְּטוֹפָתִ֖י לַזַּרְחִ֑י וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ ס
עַשְׁתֵּֽי־עָשָׂר֙ לְעַשְׁתֵּ֣י עָשָׂ֣ר הַחֹ֔דֶשׁ בְּנָיָ֥ה הַפִּרְעָתוֹנִ֖י מִן־בְּנֵ֣י אֶפְרָ֑יִם וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ ס
הַשְּׁנֵ֤ים עָשָׂר֙ לִשְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֣ר הַחֹ֔דֶשׁ חֶלְדַּ֥י הַנְּטוֹפָתִ֖י לְעׇתְנִיאֵ֑ל וְעַל֙ מַחֲלֻקְתּ֔וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ פ
וְעַל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָראוּבֵנִ֣י נָגִ֔יד אֱלִיעֶ֖זֶר בֶּן־זִכְרִ֑י {ס}        לַשִּׁ֨מְעוֹנִ֔י שְׁפַטְיָ֖הוּ בֶּֽן־מַעֲכָֽה׃ ס
לְלֵוִ֛י חֲשַׁבְיָ֥ה בֶן־קְמוּאֵ֖ל לְאַהֲרֹ֥ן צָדֽוֹק׃ ס
לִיהוּדָ֕ה אֱלִיה֖וּ מֵאֲחֵ֣י דָוִ֑יד {ס}        לְיִ֨שָּׂשכָ֔ר עׇמְרִ֖י בֶּן־מִיכָאֵֽל׃ ס
לִזְבוּלֻ֕ן יִֽשְׁמַעְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־עֹבַדְיָ֑הוּ {ס}        לְנַ֨פְתָּלִ֔י יְרִימ֖וֹת בֶּן־עַזְרִיאֵֽל׃ ס
לִבְנֵ֣י אֶפְרַ֔יִם הוֹשֵׁ֖עַ בֶּן־עֲזַזְיָ֑הוּ לַֽחֲצִי֙ שֵׁ֣בֶט מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה יוֹאֵ֖ל בֶּן־פְּדָיָֽהוּ׃ ס
לַֽחֲצִ֤י הַֽמְנַשֶּׁה֙ גִּלְעָ֔דָה יִדּ֖וֹ בֶּן־זְכַרְיָ֑הוּ {ס}        לְבִ֨נְיָמִ֔ן יַעֲשִׂיאֵ֖ל בֶּן־אַבְנֵֽר׃ ס
לְדָ֕ן עֲזַרְאֵ֖ל בֶּן־יְרֹחָ֑ם אֵ֕לֶּה שָׂרֵ֖י שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
וְלֹֽא־נָשָׂ֤א דָוִיד֙ מִסְפָּרָ֔ם לְמִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּלְמָ֑טָּה כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֔ה לְהַרְבּ֥וֹת אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כְּכוֹכְבֵ֥י הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
יוֹאָ֨ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֜ה הֵחֵ֤ל לִמְנוֹת֙ וְלֹ֣א כִלָּ֔ה וַיְהִ֥י בָזֹ֛את קֶ֖צֶף עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֤א עָלָה֙ הַמִּסְפָּ֔ר בְּמִסְפַּ֥ר דִּבְרֵֽי־הַיָּמִ֖ים לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִֽיד׃ ס
וְעַל֙ אֹצְר֣וֹת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַזְמָ֖וֶת בֶּן־עֲדִיאֵ֑ל {ס}        וְעַ֣ל הָאֹצָר֡וֹת בַּשָּׂדֶ֞ה בֶּֽעָרִ֤ים וּבַכְּפָרִים֙ וּבַמִּגְדָּל֔וֹת יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן בֶּן־עֻזִּיָּֽהוּ׃ ס
וְעַ֗ל עֹשֵׂי֙ מְלֶ֣אכֶת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה לַעֲבֹדַ֖ת הָאֲדָמָ֑ה עֶזְרִ֖י בֶּן־כְּלֽוּב׃ ס
וְעַ֨ל־הַכְּרָמִ֔ים שִׁמְעִ֖י הָרָמָתִ֑י {ס}        וְעַ֤ל שֶׁבַּכְּרָמִים֙ לְאֹצְר֣וֹת הַיַּ֔יִן זַבְדִּ֖י הַשִּׁפְמִֽי׃ ס
וְעַל־הַזֵּיתִ֤ים וְהַשִּׁקְמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשְּׁפֵלָ֔ה בַּ֥עַל חָנָ֖ן הַגְּדֵרִ֑י {ס}        וְעַל־אֹצְר֥וֹת הַשֶּׁ֖מֶן יוֹעָֽשׁ׃ ס
וְעַל־הַבָּקָר֙ הָרֹעִ֣ים בַּשָּׁר֔וֹן (שטרי) [שִׁרְטַ֖י] הַשָּׁרוֹנִ֑י {ס}        וְעַל־הַבָּקָר֙ בָּעֲמָקִ֔ים שָׁפָ֖ט בֶּן־עַדְלָֽי׃ ס
וְעַ֨ל־הַגְּמַלִּ֔ים אוֹבִ֖יל הַיִּשְׁמְעֵלִ֑י {ס}        וְעַל־הָ֣אֲתֹנ֔וֹת יֶחְדְּיָ֖הוּ הַמֵּרֹנֹתִֽי׃ ס
וְעַל־הַצֹּ֖אן יָזִ֣יז הַהַגְרִ֑י כׇּל־אֵ֙לֶּה֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הָרְכ֔וּשׁ אֲשֶׁ֖ר לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִֽיד׃ ס
וִיהוֹנָתָ֤ן דּוֹד־דָּוִיד֙ יוֹעֵ֔ץ אִישׁ־מֵבִ֥ין וְסוֹפֵ֖ר ה֑וּא וִיחִיאֵ֥ל בֶּן־חַכְמוֹנִ֖י עִם־בְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ ס
וַאֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל יוֹעֵ֣ץ לַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְחוּשַׁ֥י הָאַרְכִּ֖י רֵ֥עַ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ ס
וְאַחֲרֵ֣י אֲחִיתֹ֗פֶל יְהוֹיָדָ֤ע בֶּן־בְּנָיָ֙הוּ֙ וְאֶבְיָתָ֔ר וְשַׂר־צָבָ֥א לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יוֹאָֽב׃ פ

וַיַּקְהֵ֣ל דָּוִ֣יד אֶת־כׇּל־שָׂרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל שָׂרֵ֣י הַשְּׁבָטִ֣ים וְשָׂרֵ֣י הַמַּחְלְק֣וֹת הַמְשָׁרְתִ֪ים אֶת־הַמֶּ֟לֶךְ וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָאֲלָפִ֣ים וְשָׂרֵ֣י הַמֵּא֡וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֣י כׇל־רְכוּשׁ־וּמִקְנֶה֩ <small>׀</small> לַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וּלְבָנָ֜יו עִם־הַסָּרִיסִ֧ים וְהַגִּבּוֹרִ֛ים וּֽלְכׇל־גִּבּ֥וֹר חָ֖יִל אֶל־יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃

וַיָּ֨קׇם דָּוִ֤יד הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ עַל־רַגְלָ֔יו וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שְׁמָע֖וּנִי אַחַ֣י וְעַמִּ֑י אֲנִ֣י עִם־לְבָבִ֡י לִבְנוֹת֩ בֵּ֨ית מְנוּחָ֜ה לַאֲר֣וֹן בְּרִית־יְהֹוָ֗ה וְלַֽהֲדֹם֙ רַגְלֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ וַהֲכִינ֖וֹתִי לִבְנֽוֹת׃
וְהָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אָ֣מַר לִ֔י לֹא־תִבְנֶ֥ה בַ֖יִת לִשְׁמִ֑י כִּ֣י אִ֧ישׁ מִלְחָמ֛וֹת אַ֖תָּה וְדָמִ֥ים שָׁפָֽכְתָּ׃

וַיִּבְחַ֡ר יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵי֩ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל בִּ֜י מִכֹּ֣ל בֵּית־אָבִ֗י לִהְי֨וֹת לְמֶ֤לֶךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְעוֹלָ֔ם כִּ֤י בִֽיהוּדָה֙ בָּחַ֣ר לְנָגִ֔יד וּבְבֵ֥ית יְהוּדָ֖ה בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑י וּבִבְנֵ֣י אָבִ֔י בִּ֣י רָצָ֔ה לְהַמְלִ֖יךְ עַל־כׇּל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
וּמִ֨כׇּל־בָּנַ֔י כִּ֚י רַבִּ֣ים בָּנִ֔ים נָ֥תַן לִ֖י יְהֹוָ֑ה וַיִּבְחַר֙ בִּשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנִ֔י לָשֶׁ֗בֶת עַל־כִּסֵּ֛א מַלְכ֥וּת יְהֹוָ֖ה עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לִ֔י שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בִנְךָ֔ הוּא־יִבְנֶ֥ה בֵיתִ֖י וַחֲצֵרוֹתָ֑י כִּֽי־בָחַ֨רְתִּי ב֥וֹ לִי֙ לְבֵ֔ן וַאֲנִ֖י אֶהְיֶה־לּ֥וֹ לְאָֽב׃
וַהֲכִינוֹתִ֥י אֶת־מַלְכוּת֖וֹ עַד־לְעוֹלָ֑ם אִם־יֶחֱזַ֗ק לַעֲשׂ֛וֹת מִצְוֺתַ֥י וּמִשְׁפָּטַ֖י כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

וְ֠עַתָּ֠ה לְעֵינֵ֨י כׇל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל קְהַל־יְהֹוָה֙ וּבְאׇזְנֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ שִׁמְר֣וּ וְדִרְשׁ֔וּ כׇּל־מִצְוֺ֖ת יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם לְמַ֤עַן תִּֽירְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה וְהִנְחַלְתֶּ֛ם לִבְנֵיכֶ֥ם אַחֲרֵיכֶ֖ם עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

וְאַתָּ֣ה שְׁלֹמֹֽה־בְנִ֡י דַּע֩ אֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֨י אָבִ֜יךָ וְעׇבְדֵ֗הוּ בְּלֵ֤ב שָׁלֵם֙ וּבְנֶ֣פֶשׁ חֲפֵצָ֔ה כִּ֤י כׇל־לְבָבוֹת֙ דּוֹרֵ֣שׁ יְהֹוָ֔ה וְכׇל־יֵ֥צֶר מַחֲשָׁב֖וֹת מֵבִ֑ין אִֽם־תִּדְרְשֶׁ֙נּוּ֙ יִמָּ֣צֵא לָ֔ךְ וְאִם־תַּעַזְבֶ֖נּוּ יַזְנִיחֲךָ֥ לָעַֽד׃
רְאֵ֣ה ׀ עַתָּ֗ה כִּֽי־יְהֹוָ֛ה בָּ֧חַר בְּךָ֛ לִבְנֽוֹת־בַּ֥יִת לַמִּקְדָּ֖שׁ חֲזַ֥ק וַעֲשֵֽׂה׃ פ
וַיִּתֵּ֣ן דָּוִ֣יד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֡וֹ אֶת־תַּבְנִ֣ית הָאוּלָם֩ וְֽאֶת־בָּ֨תָּ֜יו וְגַנְזַכָּ֧יו וַעֲלִיֹּתָ֛יו וַחֲדָרָ֥יו הַפְּנִימִ֖ים וּבֵ֥ית הַכַּפֹּֽרֶת׃
וְתַבְנִ֗ית כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה בָר֙וּחַ֙ עִמּ֔וֹ לְחַצְר֧וֹת בֵּית־יְהֹוָ֛ה וּלְכׇל־הַלְּשָׁכ֖וֹת סָבִ֑יב לְאֹֽצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּלְאֹצְר֖וֹת הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים׃
וּֽלְמַחְלְקוֹת֙ הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם וּֽלְכׇל־מְלֶ֖אכֶת עֲבוֹדַ֣ת בֵּית־יְהֹוָ֑ה וּֽלְכׇל־כְּלֵ֖י עֲבוֹדַ֥ת בֵּית־יְהֹוָֽה׃
לַזָּהָ֤ב בַּמִּשְׁקָל֙ לַזָּהָ֔ב לְכׇל־כְּלֵ֖י עֲבוֹדָ֣ה וַעֲבוֹדָ֑ה לְכֹ֨ל כְּלֵ֤י הַכֶּ֙סֶף֙ בְּמִשְׁקָ֔ל לְכׇל־כְּלֵ֖י עֲבוֹדָ֥ה וַעֲבוֹדָֽה׃

וּמִשְׁקָ֞ל לִמְנֹר֣וֹת הַזָּהָ֗ב וְנֵרֹֽתֵיהֶם֙ זָהָ֔ב בְּמִשְׁקַל־מְנוֹרָ֥ה וּמְנוֹרָ֖ה וְנֵרֹתֶ֑יהָ וְלִמְנֹר֨וֹת הַכֶּ֤סֶף בְּמִשְׁקָל֙ לִמְנוֹרָ֣ה וְנֵרֹתֶ֔יהָ כַּעֲבוֹדַ֖ת מְנוֹרָ֥ה וּמְנוֹרָֽה׃
וְאֶת־הַזָּהָ֥ב מִשְׁקָ֛ל לְשֻׁלְחֲנ֥וֹת הַֽמַּעֲרֶ֖כֶת לְשֻׁלְחַ֣ן וְשֻׁלְחָ֑ן וְכֶ֖סֶף לְשֻׁלְחֲנ֥וֹת הַכָּֽסֶף׃
וְהַמִּזְלָג֧וֹת וְהַמִּזְרָק֛וֹת וְהַקְּשָׂוֺ֖ת זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וְלִכְפוֹרֵ֨י הַזָּהָ֤ב בְּמִשְׁקָל֙ לִכְפ֣וֹר וּכְפ֔וֹר וְלִכְפוֹרֵ֥י הַכֶּ֛סֶף בְּמִשְׁקָ֖ל לִכְפ֥וֹר וּכְפֽוֹר׃
וּלְמִזְבַּ֧ח הַקְּטֹ֛רֶת זָהָ֥ב מְזֻקָּ֖ק בַּמִּשְׁקָ֑ל וּלְתַבְנִ֣ית הַמֶּרְכָּבָ֗ה הַכְּרוּבִ֤ים זָהָב֙ לְפֹ֣רְשִׂ֔ים וְסֹכְכִ֖ים עַל־אֲר֥וֹן בְּרִית־יְהֹוָֽה׃
הַכֹּ֥ל בִּכְתָ֛ב מִיַּ֥ד יְהֹוָ֖ה עָלַ֣י הִשְׂכִּ֑יל כֹּ֖ל מַלְאֲכ֥וֹת הַתַּבְנִֽית׃ פ

וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜יד לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנ֗וֹ חֲזַ֤ק וֶֽאֱמַץ֙ וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה אַל־תִּירָ֖א וְאַל־תֵּחָ֑ת כִּי֩ יְהֹוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֱלֹהַי֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ לֹ֤א יַרְפְּךָ֙ וְלֹ֣א יַעַזְבֶ֔ךָּ עַד־לִכְל֕וֹת כׇּל־מְלֶ֖אכֶת עֲבוֹדַ֥ת בֵּית־יְהֹוָֽה׃

וְהִנֵּ֗ה מַחְלְקוֹת֙ הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם לְכׇל־עֲבוֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֣ית הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְעִמְּךָ֨ בְכׇל־מְלָאכָ֜ה לְכׇל־נָדִ֤יב בַּֽחׇכְמָה֙ לְכׇל־עֲבוֹדָ֔ה וְהַשָּׂרִ֥ים וְכׇל־הָעָ֖ם לְכׇל־דְּבָרֶֽיךָ׃ ס
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֤יד הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לְכׇל־הַקָּהָ֔ל שְׁלֹמֹ֨ה בְנִ֥י אֶחָ֛ד בָּחַר־בּ֥וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים נַ֣עַר וָרָ֑ךְ וְהַמְּלָאכָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה כִּ֣י לֹ֤א לְאָדָם֙ הַבִּירָ֔ה כִּ֖י לַיהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִֽים׃

וּֽכְכׇל־כֹּחִ֞י הֲכִינ֣וֹתִי לְבֵית־אֱלֹהַ֗י הַזָּהָ֣ב <small>׀</small> לַ֠זָּהָ֠ב וְהַכֶּ֨סֶף לַכֶּ֜סֶף וְהַנְּחֹ֣שֶׁת לַנְּחֹ֗שֶׁת הַבַּרְזֶל֙ לַבַּרְזֶ֔ל וְהָעֵצִ֖ים לָעֵצִ֑ים אַבְנֵי־שֹׁ֨הַם וּמִלּוּאִ֜ים אַבְנֵי־פ֣וּךְ וְרִקְמָ֗ה וְכֹ֨ל אֶ֧בֶן יְקָרָ֛ה וְאַבְנֵי־שַׁ֖יִשׁ לָרֹֽב׃
וְע֗וֹד בִּרְצוֹתִי֙ בְּבֵ֣ית אֱלֹהַ֔י יֶשׁ־לִ֥י סְגֻלָּ֖ה זָהָ֣ב וָכָ֑סֶף נָתַ֤תִּי לְבֵית־אֱלֹהַי֙ לְמַ֔עְלָה מִכׇּל־הֲכִינ֖וֹתִי לְבֵ֥ית הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
שְׁלֹ֧שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֛ים כִּכְּרֵ֥י זָהָ֖ב מִזְּהַ֣ב אוֹפִ֑יר וְשִׁבְעַ֨ת אֲלָפִ֤ים כִּכַּר־כֶּ֙סֶף֙ מְזֻקָּ֔ק לָט֖וּחַ קִיר֥וֹת הַבָּתִּֽים׃
לַזָּהָ֤ב לַזָּהָב֙ וְלַכֶּ֣סֶף לַכֶּ֔סֶף וּלְכׇל־מְלָאכָ֖ה בְּיַ֣ד חָרָשִׁ֑ים וּמִ֣י מִתְנַדֵּ֔ב לְמַלֹּ֥אות יָד֛וֹ הַיּ֖וֹם לַיהֹוָֽה׃
וַיִּֽתְנַדְּבוּ֩ שָׂרֵ֨י הָאָב֜וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֣י ׀ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְשָׂרֵ֤י הָאֲלָפִים֙ וְהַמֵּא֔וֹת וּלְשָׂרֵ֖י מְלֶ֥אכֶת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

וַֽיִּתְּנ֞וּ לַעֲבוֹדַ֣ת בֵּית־הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים זָהָ֞ב כִּכָּרִ֣ים חֲמֵשֶׁת־אֲלָפִים֮ וַאֲדַרְכֹנִ֣ים רִבּוֹ֒ וְכֶ֗סֶף כִּכָּרִים֙ עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת אֲלָפִ֔ים וּנְחֹ֕שֶׁת רִבּ֛וֹ וּשְׁמוֹנַ֥ת אֲלָפִ֖ים כִּכָּרִ֑ים וּבַרְזֶ֖ל מֵאָה־אֶ֥לֶף כִּכָּרִֽים׃
וְהַנִּמְצָ֤א אִתּוֹ֙ אֲבָנִ֔ים נָתְנ֖וּ לְאוֹצַ֣ר בֵּית־יְהֹוָ֑ה עַ֥ל יַד־יְחִיאֵ֖ל הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּֽי׃
וַיִּשְׂמְח֤וּ הָעָם֙ עַל־הִֽתְנַדְּבָ֔ם כִּ֚י בְּלֵ֣ב שָׁלֵ֔ם הִֽתְנַדְּב֖וּ לַֽיהֹוָ֑ה וְגַם֙ דָּוִ֣יד הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שָׂמַ֖ח שִׂמְחָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃ פ
וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ דָּוִיד֙ אֶת־יְהֹוָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י כׇּל־הַקָּהָ֑ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗יד בָּר֨וּךְ אַתָּ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל אָבִ֔ינוּ מֵעוֹלָ֖ם וְעַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
לְךָ֣ יְ֠הֹוָ֠ה הַגְּדֻלָּ֨ה וְהַגְּבוּרָ֤ה וְהַתִּפְאֶ֙רֶת֙ וְהַנֵּ֣צַח וְהַה֔וֹד כִּי־כֹ֖ל בַּשָּׁמַ֣יִם וּבָאָ֑רֶץ לְךָ֤ יְהֹוָה֙ הַמַּמְלָכָ֔ה וְהַמִּתְנַשֵּׂ֖א לְכֹ֥ל <small>׀</small> לְרֹֽאשׁ׃
וְהָעֹ֤שֶׁר וְהַכָּבוֹד֙ מִלְּפָנֶ֔יךָ וְאַתָּה֙ מוֹשֵׁ֣ל בַּכֹּ֔ל וּבְיָדְךָ֖ כֹּ֣חַ וּגְבוּרָ֑ה וּבְיָ֣דְךָ֔ לְגַדֵּ֥ל וּלְחַזֵּ֖ק לַכֹּֽל׃
וְעַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ מוֹדִ֥ים אֲנַ֖חְנוּ לָ֑ךְ וּֽמְהַלְלִ֖ים לְשֵׁ֥ם תִּפְאַרְתֶּֽךָ׃
וְכִ֨י מִ֤י אֲנִי֙ וּמִ֣י עַמִּ֔י כִּי־נַעְצֹ֣ר כֹּ֔חַ לְהִתְנַדֵּ֖ב כָּזֹ֑את כִּי־מִמְּךָ֣ הַכֹּ֔ל וּמִיָּדְךָ֖ נָתַ֥נּוּ לָֽךְ׃
כִּֽי־גֵרִ֨ים אֲנַ֧חְנוּ לְפָנֶ֛יךָ וְתוֹשָׁבִ֖ים כְּכׇל־אֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ כַּצֵּ֧ל <small>׀</small> יָמֵ֛ינוּ עַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ וְאֵ֥ין מִקְוֶֽה׃
יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ כֹּ֣ל הֶהָמ֤וֹן הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֲכִינֹ֔נוּ לִבְנֽוֹת־לְךָ֥ בַ֖יִת לְשֵׁ֣ם קׇדְשֶׁ֑ךָ מִיָּדְךָ֥ (היא) [ה֖וּא] וּלְךָ֥ הַכֹּֽל׃

וְיָדַ֣עְתִּי אֱלֹהַ֔י כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ בֹּחֵ֣ן לֵבָ֔ב וּמֵישָׁרִ֖ים תִּרְצֶ֑ה אֲנִ֗י בְּיֹ֤שֶׁר לְבָבִי֙ הִתְנַדַּ֣בְתִּי כׇל־אֵ֔לֶּה וְעַתָּ֗ה עַמְּךָ֙ הַנִּמְצְאוּ־פֹ֔ה רָאִ֥יתִי בְשִׂמְחָ֖ה לְהִֽתְנַדֶּב־לָֽךְ׃
יְהֹוָ֗ה אֱ֠לֹהֵ֠י אַבְרָהָ֞ם יִצְחָ֤ק וְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ שׇׁמְרָה־זֹּ֣את לְעוֹלָ֔ם לְיֵ֥צֶר מַחְשְׁב֖וֹת לְבַ֣ב עַמֶּ֑ךָ וְהָכֵ֥ן לְבָבָ֖ם אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
וְלִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנִ֗י תֵּ֚ן לֵבָ֣ב שָׁלֵ֔ם לִשְׁמוֹר֙ מִצְוֺתֶ֔יךָ עֵדְוֺתֶ֖יךָ וְחֻקֶּ֑יךָ וְלַעֲשׂ֣וֹת הַכֹּ֔ל וְלִבְנ֖וֹת הַבִּירָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־הֲכִינֽוֹתִי׃ פ
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִיד֙ לְכׇל־הַקָּהָ֔ל בָּ֥רְכוּ נָ֖א אֶת־יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֑ם וַיְבָרְכ֣וּ כׇֽל־הַקָּהָ֗ל לַֽיהֹוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּקְּד֧וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֛וּ לַיהֹוָ֖ה וְלַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

וַיִּזְבְּח֣וּ לַיהֹוָ֣ה <small>׀</small> זְ֠בָחִ֠ים וַיַּעֲל֨וּ עֹל֜וֹת לַיהֹוָ֗ה לְֽמׇחֳרַת֮ הַיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒ פָּרִ֨ים אֶ֜לֶף אֵלִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף כְּבָשִׂ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף וְנִסְכֵּיהֶ֑ם וּזְבָחִ֥ים לָרֹ֖ב לְכׇל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
וַיֹּאכְל֨וּ וַיִּשְׁתּ֜וּ לִפְנֵ֧י יְהֹוָ֛ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בְּשִׂמְחָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וַיַּמְלִ֤יכוּ שֵׁנִית֙ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בֶן־דָּוִ֔יד וַיִּמְשְׁח֧וּ לַיהֹוָ֛ה לְנָגִ֖יד וּלְצָד֥וֹק לְכֹהֵֽן׃
וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב שְׁ֠לֹמֹ֠ה עַל־כִּסֵּ֨א יְהֹוָ֧ה <small>׀</small> לְמֶ֛לֶךְ תַּחַת־דָּוִ֥יד אָבִ֖יו וַיַּצְלַ֑ח וַיִּשְׁמְע֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו כׇּל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
וְכׇל־הַשָּׂרִים֙ וְהַגִּבֹּרִ֔ים וְגַ֕ם כׇּל־בְּנֵ֖י הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑יד נָ֣תְנוּ יָ֔ד תַּ֖חַת שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
וַיְגַדֵּ֨ל יְהֹוָ֤ה אֶת־שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לְמַ֔עְלָה לְעֵינֵ֖י כׇּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּתֵּ֤ן עָלָיו֙ ה֣וֹד מַלְכ֔וּת אֲ֠שֶׁ֠ר לֹא־הָיָ֧ה עַל־כׇּל־מֶ֛לֶךְ לְפָנָ֖יו עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ פ
וְדָוִיד֙ בֶּן־יִשָׁ֔י מָלַ֖ךְ עַל־כׇּל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
וְהַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר מָלַךְ֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה בְּחֶבְר֤וֹן מָלַךְ֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים וּבִירוּשָׁלַ֥͏ִם מָלַ֖ךְ שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְשָׁלֽוֹשׁ׃
וַיָּ֙מׇת֙ בְּשֵׂיבָ֣ה טוֹבָ֔ה שְׂבַ֥ע יָמִ֖ים עֹ֣שֶׁר וְכָב֑וֹד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
וְדִבְרֵי֙ דָּוִ֣יד הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְהָאַחֲרֹנִ֑ים הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־דִּבְרֵי֙ שְׁמוּאֵ֣ל הָרֹאֶ֔ה וְעַל־דִּבְרֵי֙ נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֔יא וְעַל־דִּבְרֵ֖י גָּ֥ד הַחֹזֶֽה׃
עִ֥ם כׇּל־מַלְכוּת֖וֹ וּגְבוּרָת֑וֹ וְהָעִתִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָבְר֤וּ עָלָיו֙ וְעַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְעַ֖ל כׇּל־מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָאֲרָצֽוֹת׃ פ
en: Adam, Shet, Enosh;
Keinan, Mahalalel, Yered;
Chanoch, Metushelach, Lemech;
Noach, Shem, Cham, and Yefet.
aWith vv. 5–23, cf. Bereshit 10.1–30.The sons of Yefet: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Yavan, Tuval, Meshech, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Difat, and Togarmah.
The sons of Yavan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kitim, and Rodanim.
The sons of Cham: Kush, Mitzrayim, Put, and Kenaan.
The sons of Kush: Seba, Chavilah, Savta, Rama, and Savtecha. The sons of Rama: Sheva and Dedan.
Kush begot Nimrod; he was the first mighty one on earth.
Mitzrayim begot the Ludim, the Anamim, the Lehavim, the Naftuchim,
the Patrusim, the Kasluchim (whence the Plishtim came forth), and the Kaftorim.
Kenaan begot Tzidon his first-born, and Chet,
and the Yevusi, the Emori, the Girgashi,
the Chivi, the Arki, the Sini,
the Arvadi, the Tzmari, and the Chamati.
The sons of Shem: Eilam, Ashur, Arpachshad, Lud, Aram, Utz, Chul, Geter, and Meshech.
Arpachshad begot Shelah; and Shelah begot Ever.
Two sons were born to Ever: the name of the one was Peleg (for in his days the earth was divided), and the name of his brother Yoktan.
Yoktan begot Almodad, Shalef, Chatzarmavet, Yarach,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
Eival, Avimael, Sheva,
Ofir, Chavilah, and Yovav; all these were the sons of Yoktan.
Shem, Arpachshad, Shelah;
Ever, Peleg, Reu;
Srug, Nachor, Terach;
Avram, that is, Avraham.
bWith vv. 28–33, cf. Bereshit 25.1–16.The sons of Avraham: Yitzchak and Yishmael.
This is their line: The first-born of Yishmael, Nevayot; and Kedar, Adbe'el, Mivsam,
Mishma, Dumah, Masa, Hadad, Teima,
Yetur, Nafish, and Kedmah. These are the sons of Yishmael.
The sons of Keturah, Avraham’s concubine: she bore Zimran, Yokshan, Medan, Midyan, Yishbak, and Shuach. The sons of Yokshan: Sheva and Dedan.
The sons of Midyan: Eifah, Efer, Chanoch, Avida, and Elda'ah. All these were the descendants of Keturah.
Avraham begot Yitzchak. The sons of Yitzchak: Esav and Yisrael.
The sons of Esav: Elifaz, Reuel, Yeush, Yalam, and Korach.
The sons of Elifaz: Teiman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Knaz, Timna, and Amalek.
The sons of Reuel: Nachat, Zerach, Shamah, and Mizah.
The sons of Seir: Lotan, Shoval, Tzivon, Anah, Dishan, Etzer, and Dishan.
The sons of Lotan: Chori and Homam; and Lotan’s sister was Timna.
The sons of Shoval: Alian, Manachat, Eival, Shephi, and Onam. The sons of Tzivon: Ayah and Anah.
The sons of Anah: Dishan. The sons of Dishan: Hamran, Eshban, Yitran, and Kran.
The sons of Etzer: Bilhan, Za'avan, and Ya'akan. The sons of Dishan: Utz and Aran.
cWith vv. 43–50, cf. Bereshit 36.31–43.These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over Bnei Yisrael: Bela son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dinhavah.
When Bela died, Yovav son of Zerach from Botzrah succeeded him as king.
When Yovav died, Chusham of the land of the Teimani succeeded him as king.
When Chusham died, Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated the Midyanim in the country of Moav, succeeded him as king, and the name of his city was Avit.
When Hadad died, Samlah of Masrekah succeeded him as king.
When Samlah died, Shaul of Rehoboth-on-the-River succeeded him as king.
When Shaul died, Ba'al Chanan son of Achbor succeeded him as king.
When Ba'al Chanan died, Hadad succeeded him as king; and the name of his city was Pai, and his wife’s name Meheitavel daughter of Matred daughter of Mei Zahav.

And Hadad died.
The clans of Edom were the clans of Timna, Alvah, Yetet,
Oholivamah, Elah, Pinon,
Knaz, Teiman, Mivtzar,
Magdiel, and Iram; these are the clans of Edom.
These are the sons of Yisrael: Reuven, Shimon, Levi, Yehudah, Yissachar, Zevulun,
Dan, Yosef, Binyamin, Naftali, Gad, and Asher.
The sons of Yehudah: Er, Onan, and Shelah; these three, Bat Shua the Kenaani woman bore to him. But Er, Yehudah’s first-born, was displeasing to Hashem, and He took his life.
His daughter-in-law Tamar also bore him Peretz and Zerach. Yehudah’s sons were five in all.
The sons of Peretz: Chetzron and Chamul.
The sons of Zerach: Zimri, Eitan, Heiman, Kalkol, and Dara, five in all.
The sons of Karmi: Achar, the troubler of Yisrael, who committed a trespass against the proscribed thing;
and Eitan’s son was Azaryah.
The sons of Chetzron that were born to him: Yerachme'el, Ram, and Kluvai.
Ram begot Aminadav, and Aminadav begot Nachshon, prince of the sons of Yehudah.
Nachshon was the father of Salma, Salma of Boaz,
Boaz of Oved, Oved of Yishai.
Yishai begot Eliav his first-born, Avinadav the second, Shima the third,
Netanel the fourth, Radai the fifth,
Otzem the sixth, David the seventh;
their sisters were Tzruyah and Avigayil. The sons of Tzruyah: Avishai, Yoav, and Asahel, three.
Avigayil bore Amasa, and the father of Amasa was Yeter the Yishmeeli.
Kalev son of Chetzron had children by his wife Azuvah, and by Yeriot; these were her sons: Jesher, Shovav, and Ardon.
When Azuvah died, Kalev married Efrat, who bore him Chur.
Chur begot Uri, and Uri begot Betzalel.
Afterward Chetzron had relations with the daughter of Machir father of Gilad—he had married her when he was sixty years old—and she bore him Sguv;
and Sguv begot Yair; he had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilad.
But Geshur and Aram took from them Chavot Yair, Knat and its dependencies, sixty towns. All these were the sons of Machir, the father of Gilad.
After the death of Chetzron, in Kalev Efratah, Aviyah, wife of Chetzron, bore Ashchur, the father of Tekoa.
The sons of Yerachme'el the first-born of Chetzron: Ram his first-born, Bunah, Oren, Otzem, and Achiyah.
Yerachme'el had another wife, whose name was Atarah; she was the mother of Onam.
The sons of Ram the first-born of Yerachme'el: Maaz, Yamin, and Eker.
The sons of Onam: Shamai and Yada. The sons of Shamai: Nadav and Avishur.
The name of Avishur’s wife was Avihayil, and she bore him Achban and Molid.
The sons of Nadav: Seled and Apayim; Seled died childless.
The sons of Apayim: Yishi. The sons of Yishi: Sheshan. The sons of Sheshan: Achlai.
The sons of Yada, Shamai’s brother: Yeter and Yehonatan; Yeter died childless.
The sons of Yehonatan: Pelet and Zaza. These were the descendants of Yerachme'el.
Sheshan had no sons, only daughters; Sheshan had a Mitzri slave, whose name was Yarcha.
So Sheshan gave his daughter in marriage to Yarcha his slave; and she bore him Atai.
Atai begot Natan, and Natan begot Zavad.
Zavad begot Eflal, and Eflal begot Oved.
Oved begot Yehu, and Yehu begot Azaryah.
Azaryah begot Cheletz, and Cheletz begot Elasah.
Elasah begot Sismai, and Sismai begot Shalum.
Shalum begot Yekamyah, and Yekamyah begot Elishama.
The sons of Kalev brother of Yerachme'el: Meshah his first-born, who was the father of Zif. The sons of Mareshah father of Chevron.
The sons of Chevron: Korach, Tapuach, Rekem, and Shema.
Shema begot Racham the father of Yorkeam, and Rekem begot Shamai.
The son of Shamai: Maon, and Maon begot Bethzur.
Eifah, Kalev’s concubine, bore Charan, Motza, and Gazez; Charan begot Gazez.
The sons of Yohdai: Regem, Yotam, Geishan, Pelet, Eifah, and Sha'af.
Ma'achah, Kalev’s concubine, bore Shever and Tirchanah.
She also bore Sha'af father of Madmanah, Sheva father of Machbenah and father of Giva; the daughter of Kalev was Achsah.

These were the descendants of Kalev.
The sons of Chur the first-born of Efratah: Shoval father of Kiryat Yearim,
Salma father of Beit Lechem, Charef father of Beit Gader.
Shoval father of Kiryat Yearim had sons: Haroeh, half of the Menuchot.
And the families of Kiryat Yearim: the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumati, and the Mishrai; from these came the Tzorati and the Eshtauli.
The sons of Salma: Beit Lechem, the Netofati, Atroth-beth-joab, and half of the Manachti, the Tzori.
The families of the scribes that dwelt at Yabetz: the Tirathites, the Shimati, the Sucathites; these are the Keini who came from Chamat, father of the house of Rechav.
These are the sons of David who were born to him in Chevron: the first-born Amnon, by Achinoam the Yizre'eli; the second Daniel, by Avigayil the Karmeli;
the third Avshalom, son of Ma'achah daughter of King Talmai of Geshur; the fourth Adoniyahu, son of Chagit;
the fifth Shfatyah, by Avital; the sixth Yitream, by his wife Eglah;
six were born to him in Chevron. He reigned there seven years and six months, and in Yerushalayim he reigned thirty-three years.
These were born to him in Yerushalayim: Shima, Shovav, Natan, and Shlomo, four by Bat Shua daughter of Amiel;
then Yivchar, Elishama, Elifelet,
Nogah, Nefeg, Yafia,
Elishama, Elyada, and Elifelet—nine.
All were David’s sons, besides the sons of the concubines; and Tamar was their sister.
The son of Shlomo: Rechavam; his son Aviyah, his son Asa, his son Yehoshafat,
his son Yoram, his son Achazyahu, his son Yoash,
his son Amatzyahu, his son Azaryah, his son Yotam,
his son Achaz, his son Chizkiyahu, his son Menashe,
his son Amon, and his son Yoshiyahu.
The sons of Yoshiyahu: Yochanan the first-born, the second Yehoyakim, the third Tzidkiyahu, the fourth Shalum.
The descendants of Yehoyakim: his son Yechonyah, his son Tzidkiyahu;
and the sons of Yechonyah, the captive: Shealtiel his son,
Malchiram, Pedayah, Shenatzar, Yekamyah, Hoshama, and Nedavyah;
the sons of Pedayah: Zerubavel and Shimi; the sons of Zerubavel: Meshulam and Chananyah, and Shlomit was their sister;
Hashubah, Ohel, Berechyah, Chasadyah, and Yushav Chesed—five.
And the sons of Chananyah: Platyahu and Yeshayah; the sons of [Yeshayah]: Refayah; the sons of [Refayah]: Arnan; the sons of [Arnan]: Ovadyah; the sons of [Ovadyah]: Shchanyah.
And the sons of Shchanyah: Shmayah; and the sons of Shmayah: Chatush, and Yigal, and Bariach, and Nearyah, and Shafat—six.
And the sons of Nearyah: Elyoeinai, and Chizkiyah, and Azrikam—three.
And the sons of Elyoeinai: Hodavyah, and Elyashiv, and Playah, and Akuv, and Yochanan, and Dlayah, and Anani—seven.
The sons of Yehudah: Peretz, Chetzron, Karmi, Chur, and Shoval.
Reayah son of Shoval begot Yachat, and Yachat begot Achumai and Lahad. These were the families of the Tzorati.
These were [the sons of] the father of Eitam: Yizre'el, Yishma, and Yidbash; and the name of their sister was Hatzlelponi,
and Penuel was the father of Gedor, and Ezer the father of Chushah. These were the sons of Chur, the first-born of Efratah, the father of Beit Lechem.
Ashchur the father of Tekoa had two wives, Chelah and Na'arah;
Na'arah bore him Achuzam, Chefer, Teimni, and Achashtari. These were the sons of Na'arah.
The sons of Chelah: Zereth, Zohar, and Etnan.
Koz was the father of Anuv, Tzovevah, and the families of Acharchel son of Harum.
Yabetz was more esteemed than his brothers; and his mother named him Yabetz, “Because,” she said, “I bore him in pain.”aHeb. ‘oṣeb, connected with “Yabetz.”
Yabetz invoked the Elokim of Yisrael, saying, “Oh, bless me, enlarge my territory, stand by me, and make me not suffer pain from misfortune!” And Elokim granted what he asked.
Kluv the brother of Shuchah begot Mechir, who was the father of Eshton.
Eshton begot Bethrapha, Paseach, and Techinah father of Ir Nachash. These were the men of Recah.
The sons of Knaz: Otniel and Srayah; and the sons of Otniel: Hathath
and Meonotai. He begot Ofrah. Srayah begot Yoav father of Gei Charashim,bLit. “the valley of the craftsmen.” so-called because they were craftsmen.
The sons of Kalev son of Yefuneh: Iru, Elah, and Naam; and the sons of Elah: Knaz.
The sons of Yehalelel: Zif, Zifah, Tirya, and Asarel.
The sons of Ezrah: Yeter, Mered, Efer, and Yalon. ShecApparently Bityah; cf. v. 18. conceived and bore Miriam, Shamai, and Yishbach father of Eshtemoa.
And his Yehudi wife bore Jered father of Gedor, Chever father of Socho, and Yekutiel father of Zanoach. These were the sons of Bityah daughter of Paroh, whom Mered married.
The sons of the wife of Hodiyah sister of Nacham were the fathers of Keilah the Garmi and Eshtemoa the Maachati.
The sons of Shimon: Amnon, Rinah, Ben Chanan, and Tilon. The sons of Yishi: Zoheth and Ben-zoheth.
The sons of Shelah son of Yehudah: Er father of Lecah, Ladah father of Mareshah, and the families of the linen factory at Beth-ashbea;
and Yokim, and the men of Kozeva and Yoash, and Saraf, who married into Moav and Yashuvi Lehem (the records are ancient).
These were the potters who dwelt at Netaim and Gederah; they dwelt there in the king’s service.
The sons of Shimon: Nemuel, Yamin, Yariv, Zerach, Shaul;
his son Shalum, his son Mivsam, his son Mishma.
The sons of Mishma: his son Chamuel, his son Zakur, his son Shimi.
Shimi had sixteen sons and six daughters; but his brothers had not many children; in all, their families were not as prolific as Bnei Yehudah.
They dwelt in Beer Sheva, Moladah, Chatzar Shual,
Bilhah, Atzem, Tolad,
Betuel, Chormah, Tziklag,
Beit Hamarkavot, Chatzar Susim, Beth-biri, and Sha'arayim. These were their towns until David became king,
together with their villages, Eitam, Ayin, Rimon, Tochen, and Ashan—five towns,

along with all their villages that were around these towns as far as Ba'al; such were their settlements.
Registered in their genealogy were:
Meshobab, Yamlech, Yoshah son of Amatzyahu,
Yoel, Yehu son of Yoshivyah son of Srayah son of Asiel.
Elyoeinai, Ya'akovah, Yeshochayah, Asayah, Adiel, Yesimiel, Bnayahu,
Ziza son of Shifi son of Alon son of Yedayah son of Shimri son of Shmayah—
these mentioned by name were chiefs in their families, and their clans increased greatly.
They went to the approaches to Gedor, to the eastern side of the valley, in search of pasture for their flocks.
They found rich, good pasture, and the land was ample, quiet, and peaceful. The former inhabitants were of Cham;

those recorded by name came in the days of King Chizkiyahu of Yehudah, and attacked their encampments and the Me'unim who were found there, and wiped them out forever, and settled in their place, because there was pasture there for their flocks.
And some of them, five hundred of the Shimoni, went to Mount Seir, with Platyahu, Nearyah, Refayah, and Uziel, sons of Yishi, at their head,
and they destroyed the last surviving Amaleki, and they live there to this day.

The sons of Reuven the first-born of Yisrael. (He was the first-born; but when he defiled his father’s bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Yosef son of Yisrael, so he is not reckoned as first-born in the genealogy;
though Yehudah became more powerful than his brothers and a leader came from him, yet the birthright belonged to Yosef.)
The sons of Reuven, the first-born of Yisrael: Chanoch, Palu, Chetzron, and Karmi.
The sons of Yoel: his son Shmayah, his son Gog, his son Shimi,
his son Michah, his son Reayah, his son Ba'al,
his son Be'erah—whom King Tilgat Pilneser of Ashur exiled—was chieftain of the Reuveni.
And his kinsmen, by their families, according to their lines in the genealogy: the head, Yeiel, and Zecharyah,
and Bela son of Azaz son of Shema son of Yoel; he dwelt in Aroer as far as Nevo and Ba'al Meon.
He also dwelt to the east as far as the fringe of the wilderness this side of the Perat, because their cattle had increased in the land of Gilad.
And in the days of Shaul they made war on the Hagri'im, who fell by their hand; and they occupied their tents throughout all the region east of Gilad.
The sons of Gad dwelt facing them in the land of Bashan as far as Salchah:
Yoel the chief, Shafam the second, Yanai, and Shafat in Bashan.
And by clans: Michael, Meshulam, Sheva, Yorai, Yakan, Zia, and Ever—seven.
These were the sons of Avihayil son of Churi son of Yaroach son of Gilad son of Michael son of Yeshishai son of Yachdo son of Buz;
Ahi son of Abdiel son of Guni was chief of their clan,
and they dwelt in Gilad, in Bashan, and in its dependencies, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon, to their limits.
All of them were registered by genealogies in the days of King Yotam of Yehudah, and in the days of King Yerovam of Yisrael.
The Reuveni, the Gadi, and the half-tribe of Menashe had warriors who carried shield and sword, drew the bow, and were experienced at war—44,760, ready for service.
They made war on the Hagri'im—Yetur, Nafish, and Nodav.

They prevailed against them; the Hagri'im and all who were with them were delivered into their hands, for they cried to Elokim in the battle, and He responded to their entreaty because they trusted in Him.
They carried off their livestock: 50,000 of their camels, 250,000 sheep, 2,000 asses, and 100,000 people.
For many fell slain, because it was Elokim’s battle. And they dwelt in their place until the exile.
The members of the half-tribe of Menashe dwelt in the land; they were very numerous from Bashan to Ba'al Chermon, Snir, and Mount Chermon.
These were the chiefs of their clans: Efer, Yishi, Eliel, Azriel, Yirmiyahu, Hodavyah, and Yachdiel, men of substance, famous men, chiefs of their clans.
But they trespassed against the Elokim of their fathers by going astray after the gods of the peoples of the land, whom Elokim had destroyed before them.

So the Elokim of Yisrael roused the spirit of King Pul of Ashur—the spirit of King Tilgat Pilneser of Ashur—and he carried them away, namely, the Reuveni, the Gadi, and the half-tribe of Menashe, and brought them to Chlach, Chavor, Hara, and the river Gozan, to this day.
aIn some editions, chap. 6 begins here.The sons of Levi: Gershom, Kehat, and Merari.
The sons of Kehat: Amram, Yitzhar, Chevron, and Uziel.
The children of Amram: Aharon, Moshe, and Miriam. The sons of Aharon: Nadav, Avihu, Elazar, and Itamar.
Elazar begot Pinchas, Pinchas begot Avishua,
Avishua begot Buki, Buki begot Uzi,
Uzi begot Zrachyah, Zrachyah begot Merayot,
Merayot begot Amaryah, Amaryah begot Achituv,
Achituv begot Tzadok, Tzadok begot Achima'atz,
Achima'atz begot Azaryah, Azaryah begot Yochanan,
and Yochanan begot Azaryah (it was he who served as priest in the House that Shlomo built in Yerushalayim).
Azaryah begot Amaryah, Amaryah begot Achituv,
Achituv begot Tzadok, Tzadok begot Shalum,
Shalum begot Chilkiyahu, Chilkiyahu begot Azaryah,
Azaryah begot Srayah, Srayah begot Yehotzadak;
and Yehotzadak went into exile when Hashem exiled Yehudah and Yerushalayim by the hand of Nevuchadnetzar.
The sons of Levi: Gershom, Kehat, and Merari.
And these are the names of the sons of Gershom: Livni and Shimi.
The sons of Kehat: Amram, Yitzhar, Chevron, and Uziel.
The sons of Merari: Machli and Mushi. These were the families of the Leviyim according to their clans.
Of Gershom: his son Livni, his son Yachat, his son Zimah,
his son Yoach, his son Ido, his son Zerach, his son Yeotrai.
The sons of Kehat: his son Aminadav, his son Korach, his son Asir,
his son Elkanah, his son Evyasaf, his son Asir,
his son Tachat, his son Uriel, his son Uziyahu, and his son Shaul.
The sons of Elkanah: Amasai and Achimot,
his son Elkanah, his son Zophai, his son Nachat,
his son Eliav, his son Yerocham, his son Elkanah.
The sons of Shmuel: his first-born aSome ancient vv. read “Yoel, and the second”; cf. Shmuel I 8.2.Vashni, and-a Aviyah.
The sons of Merari: Machli, his son Livni, his son Shimi, his son Uzah,
his son Shima, his son Chagiyah, and his son Asayah.
These were appointed by David to be in charge of song in the House of Hashem, from the time the Ark came to rest.
They served at the Tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting with song until Shlomo built the House of Hashem in Yerushalayim; and they carried out their duties as prescribed for them.
Those were the appointed men; and their sons were: Bnei Kehat: Heiman the singer, son of Yoel son of Shmuel
son of Elkanah son of Yerocham son of Eliel son of Toach
son of Tzuf son of Elkanah son of Machat son of Amasai
son of Elkanah son of Yoel son of Azaryah son of Tzefanyah
son of Tachat son of Asir son of Evyasaf son of Korach
son of Yitzhar son of Kehat son of Levi son of Yisrael;
and his kinsman Asaf, who stood on his right, namely, Asaf son of Berechyah son of Shima
son of Michael son of Ba'aseyah son of Malkiyah
son of Etni son of Zerach son of Adayah
son of Eitan son of Zimah son of Shimi
son of Yachat son of Gershom son of Levi.
On the left were their kinsmen: the sons of Merari: Eitan son of Kishi son of Avdi son of Maluch
son of Chashavyah son of Amatzyahu son of Chilkiyahu
son of Amtzi son of Bani son of Shamer
son of Machli son of Mushi son of Merari son of Levi;
and their kinsmen the Leviyim were appointed for all the service of the Tabernacle of the House of Elokim.

But Aharon and his sons made offerings upon the altar of burnt offering and upon the altar of incense, performing all the tasks of the most holy place, to make atonement for Yisrael, according to all that Moshe the servant of Elokim had commanded.
These are the sons of Aharon: his son Elazar, his son Pinchas, his son Avishua,
his son Buki, his son Uzi, his son Zrachyah,
his son Merayot, his son Amaryah, his son Achituv,
his son Tzadok, his son Achima'atz.

bWith vv. 24–51, cf. Yehoshua 21.3–42.These are their dwelling-places according to their settlements within their borders: to the sons of Aharon of the families of Bnei Kehat, for theirs was the [first] lot;
they gave them Chevron in the land of Yehudah and its surrounding pasturelands,
but the fields of the city and its villages they gave to Kalev son of Yefuneh.
To the sons of Aharon they gave the citiescYehoshua 21.13, “city.” of refuge: Chevron and Livnah with its pasturelands, Yatir and Eshtemoa with its pasturelands,
Hilen with its pasturelands, Dvir with its pasturelands,
Ashan with its pasturelands, and Beit Shemesh with its pasturelands.
From the tribe of Binyamin, Geva with its pasturelands, Alemet with its pasturelands, and Anatot with its pasturelands. All their cities throughout their families were thirteen.
To the remaining Bnei Kehat were given by lot out of the family of the tribe, out of the half-tribe, the half of Menashe, ten cities.
To the Gershomites according to their families were allotted thirteen cities out of the tribes of Yissachar, Asher, Naftali, and Menashe in Bashan.
To Bnei Merari according to their families were allotted twelve cities out of the tribes of Reuven, Gad, and Zevulun.
So the people of Yisrael gave the Leviyim the cities with their pasturelands.
They gave them by lot out of the tribe of Bnei Yehudah these cities that are mentioned by name, and out of the tribe of the Shimoni, and out of the tribe of Bnei Binyamin.
And some of the families of the sons of Kehat had cities of their territory out of the tribe of Efraim.
They gave them the cities of refuge: Shechem with its pasturelands in the hill country of Efraim, Gezer with its pasturelands,
Yokmeam with its pasturelands, Beit Choron with its pasturelands,
Ayalon with its pasturelands, Gat Rimon with its pasturelands;
and out of the half-tribe of Menashe: Aner with its pasturelands, and Bilam with its pasturelands, for the rest of the families of Bnei Kehat.
To the Gershomites; out of the half-tribe of Menashe: Golan in Bashan with its pasturelands and Ashtarot with its pasturelands;
and out of the tribe of Yissachar: Kedesh with its pasturelands, Davrat with its pasturelands,
Ramot with its pasturelands, and Anem with its pasturelands;
out of the tribe of Asher: Mashal with its pasturelands, Avdon with its pasturelands,
Chukok with its pasturelands, and Rechov with its pasturelands;
and out of the tribe of Naftali: Kedesh in Galil with its pasturelands; Chamon with its pasturelands, and Kiryatayim with its pasturelands.
To the rest of Bnei Merari, out of the tribe of Zevulun: Rimmono with its pasturelands, Tavor with its pasturelands;
and beyond the Yarden at Yericho, on the east side of the Yarden, out of the tribe of Reuven: Betzer in the wilderness with its pasturelands, Yahatz with its pasturelands,
Kedemot with its pasturelands, and Meifa'at with its pasturelands;
and out of the tribe of Gad: Ramot in Gilad with its pasturelands, Machanayim with its pasturelands,
Cheshbon with its pasturelands, and Yazer with its pasturelands.
The sons of Yissachar: Tola, Puah, Yashuv, and Shimron—four.
The sons of Tola: Uzi, Refayah, Yeriel, Yachmai, Ibsam, Shmuel, chiefs of their clans, men of substance according to their lines; their number in the days of David was 22,600.
The sons of Uzi: Yizrachyah. And the sons of Yizrachyah: Michael, Ovadyah, Yoel, and Yishiyah—five. All of them were chiefs.
And together with them, by their lines, according to their clans, were units of the fighting force, 36,000, for they had many wives and sons.
Their kinsmen belonging to all the families of Yissachar were in all 87,000 men of substance; they were all registered by genealogy.
[The sons of] Binyamin: Bela, Becher, and Yediael—three.
The sons of Bela: Etzbon, Uzi, Uziel, Yerimot, and Iri—five, chiefs of clans, men of substance, registered by genealogy—22,034.
The sons of Becher: Zemirah, Yoash, Eliezer, Elyoeinai, Omri, Yeremot, Aviyah, Anatot, and Alemet. All these were the sons of Becher;
and they were registered by genealogy according to their lines, as chiefs of their clans, men of substance—20,200.
The sons of Yediael: Bilhan. And the sons of Bilhan: Yeush, Binyamin, Ehud, Kna'anah, Zeitan, Tarshish, and Achishachar.
All these were the sons of Yediael, chiefs of the clans, men of substance—17,200, who made up the fighting force.
And Shupim and Chupim were the sons of Ir; Chushim the sons of Acher.
The sons of Naftali: Jahziel, Guni, Yetzer, and Shalum, the descendants of Bilhah.
The sons of Menashe: Asriel, whom his Arami concubine bore; she bore Machir the father of Gilad.
And Machir took wives for Chupim and for Shupim. The name of his sister was Ma'achah. And the name of the second was Tzelofchad; and Tzelofchad had daughters.
And Ma'achah the wife of Machir bore a son, and she named him Peresh; and the name of his brother was Sharesh; and his sons were Ele and Rekem.
The sons of Ele: Bedan. These were the sons of Gilad son of Machir son of Menashe.
And his sister Hamolechet bore Ishod, Aviezer, and Machlah.
The sons of Shmida were Achyan, Shechem, Likchi, and Aniam.
The sons of Efraim: Shutelach, his son Bared, his son Tachat, his son Eladah, his son Tachat,
his son Zavad, his son Shutelach, also Ezer and Elad. The men of Gat, born in the land, killed them because they had gone down to take their cattle.
And Efraim their father mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.
He cohabited with his wife, who conceived and bore a son; and she named him Briah, because it occurred when there was misfortuneaHeb. bera‘ah. in his house.
His daughter was She'erah, who built both Lower and Upper Beit Choron, and Uzzen-sheerah.
His son Refach, his son Reshef, his son Telach, his son Tachan,
his son Ladan, his son Amihud, his son Elishama,
his son Non, his son Yehoshua.
Their possessions and settlements were Beit El and its dependencies, and on the east Na'aran, and on the west Gezer and its dependencies, Shechem and its dependencies, and Ayah and its dependencies;

also along the borders of the Menashi, Beit Shean and its dependencies, Ta'anach and its dependencies, Megiddo and its dependencies, Dor and its dependencies. In these dwelt the sons of Yosef son of Yisrael.
The sons of Asher: Yimnah, Yishvah, Yishvi, Briah, and their sister Serach.
The sons of Briah: Chever and Malkiel, who was the father of Birzaith.
Chever begot Yaflet, Shomer, Chotam, and their sister, Shua.
The sons of Yaflet: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvat. These were the sons of Yaflet.
The sons of Shamer: Ahi, Rohgah, Chubah, and Aram.
The sons of Helem his brother: Tzofach, Yimna, Shelesh, and Amal.
The sons of Tzofach: Suah, Charnefer, Shual, Beri, Yimrah,
Betzer, Hod, Shama, Shilshah, Yitran, and Be'era.
The sons of Yeter: Yefuneh, Pispah, and Ara.
The sons of Ulla: Arach, Chaniel, and Ritzya.

All of these men of Asher, chiefs of the clans, select men, men of substance, heads of the chieftains. And they were registered by genealogy according to fighting force; the number of the men was 26,000 men.
Binyamin begot Bela his first-born, Ashbel the second, Achrach the third,
Nohah the fourth, and Rafa the fifth.
And Bela had sons: Adar, Gera, Avihud,
Avishua, Naaman, Achoach,
Gera, Shephuphan, and Churam.
These were the sons of Ehud—they were chiefs of clans of the inhabitants of Geva, and they were exiled to Manachat:
Naaman, Achiyah, and Gera—he exiled them and begot Uza and Achihud.
And Shacharayim had sons in the country of Moav after he had sent away Chushim and Ba'ara his wives.
He had sons by Chodesh his wife: Yovav, Tzivya, Mesha, Malkam,
Jeuz, Sachyah, and Mirmah. These were his sons, chiefs of clans.
He also begot by Chushim: Abitub and Elpa'al.
The sons of Elpa'al: Ever, Misham, and Shamed, who built Ono and Lod with its dependencies,
and Briah and Shema—they were chiefs of clans of the inhabitants of Ayalon, who put to flight the inhabitants of Gat;
and Achyo, Shashak, and Yeremot.
Zvadyah, Arad, Eder,
Michael, Ishpah, and Yocha were sons of Briah.
Zvadyah, Meshulam, Chizki, Chever,
Ishmerai, Izliah, and Yovav were the sons of Elpa'al.
Yakim, Zichri, Zavdi,
Elienai, Tziltai, Eliel,
Adayah, Brayah, and Shimrat were the sons of Shimi.
Ishpan, Ever, Eliel,
Avdon, Zichri, Chanan,
Chananyah, Eilam, Antotiyah,
Iphdeiah, and Penuel were the sons of Shashak.
Shamsherai, Shecharyah, Atalyahu,
Jaareshiah, Eliyahu, and Zichri were the sons of Yerocham.
These were the chiefs of the clans, according to their lines. These chiefs dwelt in Yerushalayim.
The father of Givon dwelt in Givon, and the name of his wife was Ma'achah.
His first-born son: Avdon; then Tzur, Kish, Ba'al, Nadav,
Gedor, Achyo, Zacher.
Miklot begot Shimah. And they dwelt in Yerushalayim opposite their kinsmen, with their kinsmen.
Ner begot Kish, Kish begot Shaul, Shaul begot Yehonatan, Malki Shua, Avinadav, and Eshba'al;
and the son of Yehonatan was Meriv Ba'al; and Meriv Ba'al begot Michah.
The sons of Michah: Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Achaz.
Achaz begot Yehoadah; and Yehoadah begot Alemet, Azmavet, and Zimri; Zimri begot Motza.
Motza begot Bina; his son Rafah; his son Elasah, his son Atzel.
Atzel had six sons, and these are their names: Azrikam, Bochru, Yishmael, Shearyah, Ovadyah, and Chanan. All these were the sons of Atzel.
The sons of Eshek his brother: Ele his first-born, Yeush the second, and Elifelet the third.
The descendants of Ele—men of substance, who drew the bow, had many children and grandchildren—one hundred and fifty; all these were Bnei Binyamin.
All Yisrael was registered by genealogies; and these are in the book of the kings of Yisrael. And Yehudah was taken into exile in Bavel because of their trespass.
aWith vv. 2–17, cf. Nechemyah 11.3–19.The first to settle in their towns, on their property, were Bnei Yisrael, priests, Leviyim, and temple servants,
while some of Bnei Yehudah and some of Bnei Binyamin and some of Bnei Efraim and Manassehites settled in Yerushalayim;
Utai son of Amihud son of Omri son of Imri son of Bani, from the sons of Peretz son of Yehudah;
and of the Shiloni: Asayah the first-born and his sons.
Of the sons of Zerach: Jeuel and their kinsmen—690.
Of Bnei Binyamin: Sallu son of Meshulam son of Hodavyah son of Hasnuah,
Yivniyah son of Yerocham, Elah son of Uzi son of Michri, and Meshulam son of Shfatyah son of Reuel son of Yivniyah;
and their kinsmen, according to their lines—956. All these were chiefs of their ancestral clans.
Of the priests: Yedayah, Yehoyariv, Yachin,
and Azaryah son of Chilkiyahu son of Meshulam son of Tzadok son of Merayot son of Achituv, chief officer of the House of Elokim;
and Adayah son of Yerocham son of Pashchur son of Malkiyah, and Masai son of Adiel son of Yachzerah son of Meshulam son of Meshilemit son of Imer,
together with their kinsmen, chiefs of their clans—1,760, men of substance for the work of the service of the House of Elokim.
Of the Leviyim: Shmayah son of Chashuv son of Azrikam son of Chashavyah, of the sons of Merari;
and Bakbakar, Cheresh, Galal, and Matanyah son of Micha son of Zichri son of Asaf;
and Ovadyah son of Shmayah son of Galal son of Yedutun, and Berechyah son of Asa son of Elkanah, who dwelt in the villages of the Netofati.
The gatekeepers were: Shalum, Akuv, Talmon, Achiman; and their kinsman Shalum was the chief
hitherto in the King’s Gate on the east. They were the keepers belonging to the Levi camp.

Shalum son of Kore son of Evyasaf son of Korach, and his kinsmen of his clan, Bnei Korach, were in charge of the work of the service, guards of the threshold of the Tent; their fathers had been guards of the entrance to the camp of Hashem.
And Pinchas son of Elazar was the chief officer over them in time past; Hashem was with him.
Zecharyah the son of Meshelemyah was gatekeeper at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
All these, who were selected as gatekeepers at the thresholds, were 212. They were selected by genealogies in their villages. David and Shmuel the seer established them in their office of trust.
They and their descendants were in charge of the gates of the House of Hashem, that is, the House of the Tent, as guards.
The gatekeepers were on the four sides, east, west, north, and south;
and their kinsmen in their villages were obliged to join them every seven days, according to a fixed schedule.
The four chief gatekeepers, who were Leviyim, were entrusted to be over the chambers and the treasuries of the House of Elokim.
They spent the night near the House of Elokim; for they had to do guard duty, and they were in charge of opening it every morning.
Some of them had charge of the service vessels, for they were counted when they were brought back and taken out.
Some of them were in charge of the vessels and all the holy vessels, and of the flour, wine, oil, incense, and spices.
Some of the priests blended the compound of spices.
Matityahu, one of the Leviyim, the first-born of Shalum the Korahite, was entrusted with making the flat cakes.
Also some of their Kehati kinsmen had charge of the rows of bread, to prepare them for each sabbath.
Now these are the singers, the chiefs of Levitical clans who remained in the chambers free of other service, for they were on duty day and night.
These were chiefs of Levitical clans, according to their lines; these chiefs lived in Yerushalayim.
The father of Givon, Yeiel, lived in Givon, and the name of his wife was Ma'achah.
His first-born son, Avdon; then Tzur, Kish, Ba'al, Ner, Nadav,
Gedor, Achyo, Zecharyah, and Miklot;
Miklot begot Shimam; and they lived in Yerushalayim opposite their kinsmen, with their kinsmen.
Ner begot Kish, Kish begot Shaul, Shaul begot Yehonatan, Malki Shua, Avinadav, and Eshba'al;
and the son of Yehonatan was Meriv Ba'al; and Meriv Ba'al begot Michah.
The sons of Michah: Pithon, Melech, Tachrea;
Achaz begot Yarah, and Yarah begot Alemet, Azmavet, and Zimri; Zimri begot Motza.
Motza begot Bina; his son was Refayah, his son Elasah, his son Atzel.
Atzel had six sons and these were their names: Azrikam, Bochru, Yishmael, Shearyah, Ovadyah, and Chanan. These were the sons of Atzel.
aWith vv. 1–12, cf. Shmuel I 31.1–13.The Plishtim attacked Yisrael, and the men of Yisrael fled before the Plishtim and [many] fell on Mount Gilboa.
The Plishtim pursued Shaul and his sons, and the Plishtim struck down Yehonatan, Avinadav, and Malki Shua, sons of Shaul.
The battle raged around Shaul, and the archers hit him, and he bMeaning of Heb. uncertain.was wounded-b by the archers.

Shaul said to his arms-bearer, “Draw your sword and run me through, so that these uncircumcised may not come and make sport of me.” But his arms-bearer, out of great awe, refused; whereupon Shaul grasped the sword and fell upon it.
When the arms-bearer saw that Shaul was dead, he too fell on his sword and died.
Thus Shaul and his three sons and his entire house died together.

And when all the men of Yisrael who were in the valley saw that theycI.e., Yisrael. had fled and that Shaul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their towns and fled; the Plishtim then came and occupied them.
The next day the Plishtim came to strip the slain, and they found Shaul and his sons lying on Mount Gilboa.
They stripped him, and carried off his head and his armor, and sent them throughout the land of the Plishtim to spread the news to their idols and among the people.
They placed his armor in the temple of their god, and they impaled his head in the temple of Dagan.
When all Yavesh Gilad heard everything that the Plishtim had done to Shaul,
all their stalwart men set out, removed the bodies of Shaul and his sons, and brought them to Yavesh. They buried the bones under the oak tree in Yavesh, and they fasted for seven days.
Shaul died for the trespass that he had committed against Hashem in not having fulfilled the command of Hashem; moreover, he had consulted a ghost to seek advice,
and did not seek advice of Hashem; so He had him slain and the kingdom transferred to David son of Yishai.
aWith vv. 1–9, cf. Shmuel II 5.1–10, and with vv. 11–41, cf. Shmuel II 23.8–39.All Yisrael gathered to David at Chevron and said, “We are your own flesh and blood.
Long before now, even when Shaul was king, you were the leader of Yisrael; and Hashem your Elokim said to you: You shall shepherd My people Yisrael; you shall be ruler of My people Yisrael.”

All the elders of Yisrael came to the king at Chevron, and David made a pact with them in Chevron before Hashem. And they anointed David king over Yisrael, according to the word of Hashem through Shmuel.
David and all Yisrael set out for Yerushalayim, that is Yevus, where the Yevusi inhabitants of the land lived.
David was told by the inhabitants of Yevus, “You will never get in here!” But David captured the stronghold of Tziyon; it is now the City of David.
David said, “Whoever attacks the Yevusi first will be the chief officer”; Yoav son of Tzruyah attacked first, and became the chief.
David occupied the stronghold; therefore it was renamed the City of David.
David also fortified the surrounding area, from the Milo round about, and Yoav rebuilt the rest of the city.
David kept growing stronger, for Hashem of Hosts was with him.
And these were David’s chief warriors who strongly supported him in his kingdom, together with all Yisrael, to make him king, according to the word of Hashem concerning Yisrael.
This is the list of David’s warriors: Yashovam son of Chachmoni, the chief officer; he wielded his spear against three hundred and slew them all on one occasion.
Next to him was Elazar son of Dodo, the Achochi; he was one of the three warriors.
He was with David at Pas Damim when the Plishtim gathered there for battle. There was a plot of ground full of barley there; the troops had fled from the Plishtim,
but they took their stand in the middle of the plot and defended it, and they routed the Plishtim. Thus Hashem wrought a great victory.
Three of the thirty chiefs went down to the rock to David, at the cave of Adulam, while a force of Plishtim was encamped in the Valley of Refaim.
David was then in the stronghold, and a Plishti garrison was then at Beit Lechem.
David felt a craving and said, “If only I could get a drink of water from the cistern which is by the gate of Beit Lechem!”

So the three got through the Plishti camp, and drew water from the cistern which is by the gate of Beit Lechem, and they carried it back to David. But David would not drink it, and he poured it out as a libation to Hashem.

For he said, “Elokim forbid that I should do this! Can I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives?”—for they had brought it at the risk of their lives, and he would not drink it. Such were the exploits of the three warriors.
Abshai, the brother of Yoav, was head of another three. He once wielded his spear against three hundred and slew them. He won a name among the three;
among the three he was more highly regarded than the other two, and so he became their commander. However, he did not attain to the other three.
Bnayahu son of Yehoyada from Kavtze'el was a brave soldier who performed great deeds. He killed the two [sons] of Ariel of Moav. Once, on a snowy day, he went down into a pit and killed a lion.

He also killed a Mitzri, a giant of a man five cubits tall. The Mitzri had a spear in his hand, like a weaver’s beam, yet [Bnayahu] went down against him with a club, wrenched the spear out of the Mitzri’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.
Such were the exploits of Bnayahu son of Yehoyada; and he won a name among the three warriors.
He was highly regarded among the thirty, but he did not attain to the three. David put him in charge of his bodyguard.bMeaning of Heb. uncertain.
The valiant warriors: Asahel brother of Yoav, Elchanan son of Dodo from Beit Lechem,
Shammoth the Harori, Cheletz the Ploni,
Ira son of Ikesh from Tekoa, Aviezer of Anatot,
Sibchai the Chushati, Ilai the Achochi,
Mahrai the Netofati, Cheled son of Ba'anah the Netofati,
Itai son of Rivai from Givah of Bnei Binyamin, Bnayahu of Piraton,
Hurai of Nachalei Ga'ash, Aviel the Arvati,
Azmavet the Bacharumi, Elyachba of Sha'alvon,
the sons of Hashem the Gizoni, Yehonatan son of Shage the Harari,
Achiam son of Sachar the Harari, Elifal son of Ur,
Chefer the Mecherati, Achiyah the Ploni,
Hezro the Karmeli, Na'arai son of Ezbai,
Yoel brother of Natan, Mivchar son of Char,
Zelek the Amoni, Nachrai the Beroti—the arms-bearer of Yoav son of Tzruyah—
Ira the Yitri, Garev the Yitri,
Uriyah the Chiti, Zavad son of Achlai.
Adina son of Shiza the Ruveni, a chief of the Reuveni, and thirty with him;
Chanan son of Ma'achah, and Yoshafat the Mitni;
Uziyahu the Ashterati, Shama and Yeiel sons of Chotam the Aroeri;
Jedaiael son of Shimri, and Yocha his brother, the Titzi;
Eliel the Mahavite, and Yerivai and Yoshavyah sons of Elna'am, and Yitmah the Moavi;
Eliel, Oved, and Ya'asiel the Mezobaite.
The following joined David at Tziklag while he was still in hiding from Shaul son of Kish; these were the warriors who gave support in battle;
they were armed with the bow and could use both right hand and left hand to sling stones or shoot arrows with the bow; they were kinsmen of Shaul from Binyamin.
At the head were Achiezer and Yoash, sons of Shma'ah of Givah; and Yezavel and Pelet, sons of Azmavet; and Brachah and Yehu of Anatot;
Ishmaiah of Givon, a warrior among the thirty, leading the thirty;
Yirmiyahu, Yachaziel, Yochanan, and Yozavad of Gederah;
Eluzai, Yerimot, Bealyah, Shmaryah, and Shfatyah the Charufi;
Elkanah, Yishiyah, Azarel, Yoezer, and Yashovam Bnei Korach;
Joelah and Zvadyah, sons of Yerocham of Gedor.aOr, “the troop,” reading Heb. gedud with several mss.

Of the Gadi, there withdrew to follow David to the wilderness stronghold valiant men, fighters fit for battle, armed with shield and spear; they had the appearance of lions, and were as swift as gazelles upon the mountains:
Ezer the chief, Ovadyah the second, Eliav the third,
Mashmannah the fourth, Yirmiyahu the fifth,
Atai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,
Yochanan the eighth, Elzavad the ninth,
Yirmiyahu the tenth, Machbanai the eleventh.
Those were the Gadi, heads of the army. The least was equal to a hundred, the greatest to a thousand.
These were the ones who crossed the Yarden in the first month, when it was at its crest, and they put to flight all the lowlanders to the east and west.
Some of Bnei Binyamin and Bnei Yehudah came to the stronghold to David,

and David went out to meet them, saying to them, “If you come on a peaceful errand, to support me, then I will make common cause with you, but if to betray me to my foes, for no injustice on my part, then let the Elokim of our fathers take notice and give judgment.”

Then the spirit seized Amasai, chief of the captains:
“We are yours, David,
On your side, son of Yishai;
At peace, at peace with you,
And at peace with him who supports you,
For your Elokim supports you.”
So David accepted them, and placed them at the head of his band.

Some Menashi went over to David’s side when he came with the Plishtim to make war against Shaul, but they were of no help to them, because the lords of the Plishtim in council dismissed him, saying, “He will go over to the side of his lord, Shaul, and it will cost us our heads”;
when he went to Tziklag, these Menashi went over to his side—Adnah, Yozavad, Yediael, Michael, Yozavad, Elihu, and Tziltai, chiefs of the clans of Menashe.
It was they who gave support to David against the band,bI.e., the band of Amaleki raiders; cf. Shmuel I 30.8, 15. for all were valiant men; and they were officers of the force.
Day in day out, people came to David to give him support, until there was an army as vast as the army of Elokim.
These are the numbers of the [men of the] armed bands who joined David at Chevron to transfer Shaul’s kingdom to him, in accordance with the word of Hashem:
Bnei Yehudah, equipped with shield and spear—6,800 armed men;
Shimoni, valiant men, fighting troops—7,100;
of the Leviyim—4,600;
Yehoyada, chief officer of Bnei Aharon; with him, 3,700;
Tzadok, a young valiant man, with his clan—22 officers;
of Bnei Binyamin, kinsmen of Shaul, 3,000 in their great numbers, hitherto protecting the interests of the house of Shaul;
of Bnei Efraim, 20,800 valiant men, famous in their clans;
of the half-tribe of Menashe, 18,000, who were designated by name to come and make David king;
of Bnei Yissachar, men who knew how to interpret the signs of the times, to determine how Yisrael should act; their chiefs were 200, and all their kinsmen followed them;
of Zevulun, those ready for service, able to man a battle line with all kinds of weapons, 50,000, giving support wholeheartedly;
of Naftali, 1,000 chieftains with their shields and lances—37,000;
of Bnei Dan, able to man the battle line—28,600;
of Asher, those ready for service to man the battle line—40,000;
from beyond the Yarden, of the Reuveni, the Gadi, and the half-tribe of Menashe, together with all kinds of military weapons—120,000.
All these, fighting men, manning the battle line with whole heart, came to Chevron to make David king over all Yisrael. Likewise, all the rest of Yisrael was of one mind to make David king.
They were there with David three days, eating and drinking, for their kinsmen had provided for them.

And also, their relatives as far away as Yissachar, Zevulun, and Naftali brought food by ass, camel, mule, and ox—provisions of flour, cakes of figs, raisin cakes, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep in abundance, for there was joy in Yisrael.
Then David consulted with the officers of the thousands and the hundreds, with every chief officer.

David said to the entire assembly of Yisrael, “If you approve, and if Hashem our Elokim concurs,aMeaning of Heb. uncertain. let us send far and wide to our remaining kinsmen throughout the territories of Yisrael, including the priests and Leviyim in the towns where they have pasturelands, that they should gather together to us
in order to transfer the Ark of our Elokim to us, for throughout the days of Shaul we paid no regard to it.”
The entire assembly agreed to do so, for the proposal pleased all the people.
David then assembled all Yisrael from Shichor of Mitzrayim to Levo Chamat, in order to bring the Ark of Elokim from Kiryat Yearim.

bWith vv. 6–14, cf. Shmuel II 6.2–11.David and all Yisrael went up to Ba'alah, Kiryat Yearim of Yehudah, to bring up from there the Ark of Elokim, Hashem, Enthroned on the Keruvim, to which the Name was attached.
They transported the Ark of Elokim on a new cart from the house of Avinadav; Uza and Achyo guided the cart,
and David and all Yisrael danced before Elokim with all their might—with songs, lyres, harps, timbrels, cymbals, and trumpets.
But when they came to the threshing floor of Kidon, Uza put out his hand to hold the Ark of God because the oxen had stumbled.aMeaning of Heb. uncertain.
Hashem was incensed at Uza, and struck him down, because he laid a hand on the Ark; and so he died there before Elokim.
David was distressed because Hashem cHeb. paraṣ…pereṣ.had burst out-c against Uza; and that place was named Paratz Uza, as it is still called.
David was afraid of Elokim that day; he said, “How can I bring the Ark of Elokim here?”
So David did not remove the Ark to his place in the City of David; instead, he diverted it to the house of Oved Edom the Giti.
The Ark of Elokim remained in the house of Oved Edom, in its own abode, three months, and Hashem blessed the house of Oved Edom and all he had.
aWith vv. 1–16, cf. Shmuel II 5.11–25.King Chiram of Tzor sent envoys to David with cedar logs, stonemasons, and carpenters to build a palace for him.
Thus David knew that Hashem had established him as king over Yisrael, and that his kingship was highly exalted for the sake of His people Yisrael.
David took more wives in Yerushalayim, and David begot more sons and daughters.
These are the names of the children born to him in Yerushalayim:bWith the list in vv. 4–7, cf. also Divrei Hayamim I 3.5–8. Shamua, Shovav, Natan, and Shlomo;
Yivchar, Elishua, and Elpalet;
Nogah, Nefeg, and Yafia;
Elishama, Be'elyada, and Elifelet.
When the Plishtim heard that David had been anointed king over all Yisrael, all the Plishtim went up in search of David; but David heard of it, and he went out to them.
The Plishtim came and raided the Valley of Refaim.
David inquired of Elokim, “Shall I go up against the Plishtim? Will You deliver them into my hands?” And Hashem answered him, “Go up, and I will deliver them into your hands.”

Thereupon David ascended Ba'al Pratzim, and David defeated them there. David said, “Elokim cHeb. paraṣ.burst out-c against my enemies by my hands as waters burst out.” That is why that place was named Ba'al Pratzim.
They abandoned their gods there, and David ordered these to be burned.
Once again the Plishtim raided the valley.
David inquired of Elokim once more, and Elokim answered, “Do not go up after them, but circle around them and confront them at the bacadMeaning of Heb. uncertain. trees.
And when you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the baca trees, then go out to battle, for Elokim will be going in front of you to attack the Plishti forces.”
David did as Elokim had commanded him; and they routed the Plishtim from Givon all the way to Gezer.
David became famous throughout the lands, and Hashem put the fear of him in all the nations.
He had houses made for himself in the City of David, and he prepared a place for the Ark of Elokim, and pitched a tent for it.
Then David gave orders that none but the Leviyim were to carry the Ark of Elokim, for Hashem had chosen them to carry the Ark of Hashem and to minister to Him forever.
David assembled all Yisrael in Yerushalayim to bring up the Ark of Hashem to its place, which he had prepared for it.
Then David gathered together Bnei Aharon and the Leviyim:
the sons of Kehat: Uriel the officer and his kinsmen—120;
the sons of Merari: Asayah the officer and his kinsmen—220;
the sons of Gershom: Yoel the officer and his kinsmen—130;
the sons of Elitzafan: Shmayah the officer and his kinsmen—200;
the sons of Chevron: Eliel the officer and his kinsmen—80;
the sons of Uziel: Aminadav the officer and his kinsmen—112.
David sent for Tzadok and Evyatar the priests, and for the Leviyim: Uriel, Asayah, Yoel, Shmayah, Eliel, and Aminadav.
He said to them, “You are the heads of the clans of the Leviyim; sanctify yourselves, you and your kinsmen, and bring up the Ark of Hashem Elokim of Yisrael to [the place] I have prepared for it.
aMeaning of Heb. uncertain.Because you were not there the first time,-a Hashem our Elokim burst out against us, for we did not show due regard for Him.”
The priests and Leviyim sanctified themselves in order to bring up the Ark of Hashem Elokim of Yisrael.
The Leviyim carried the Ark of Elokim by means of poles on their shoulders, as Moshe had commanded in accordance with the word of Hashem.
David ordered the officers of the Leviyim to install their kinsmen, the singers, with musical instruments, harps, lyres, and cymbals, joyfully making their voices heard.
So the Leviyim installed Heiman son of Yoel and, of his kinsmen, Asaf son of Berechyah; and, of the sons of Merari their kinsmen, Eitan son of Kushayahu.

Together with them were their kinsmen of second rank, Zecharyah, Ben, Ya'aziel, Shmiramot, Yechiel, Uni, Eliav, Bnayahu, Ma'aseyah, Matityahu, Eliflehu, Mikneyahu, Oved Edom and Yeiel the gatekeepers.
Also the singers Heiman, Asaf, and Eitan to sound the bronze cymbals,
and Zecharyah, Aziel, Shmiramot, Yechiel, Uni, Eliav, Ma'aseyah, and Bnayahu with harps aMeaning of Heb. uncertain.on alamoth;-a
also Matityahu, Eliflehu, Mikneyahu, Oved Edom, Yeiel, and Azazyahu, with lyres to lead aMeaning of Heb. uncertain.on the sheminith;-a
also Knanyahu, officer of the Leviyim in song;aMeaning of Heb. uncertain. he was in charge of the songaMeaning of Heb. uncertain. because he was a master.
Berechyah and Elkanah were gatekeepers for the Ark.
Shvanyah, Yoshafat, Netanel, Amasai, Zecharyah, Bnayahu, and Eliezer the priests sounded the trumpets before the Ark of Elokim, and Obededom and Yechiyah were gatekeepers for the Ark.

bVv. 25–29 are found also in Shmuel II 6.12–16.Then David and the elders of Yisrael and the officers of the thousands who were going to bring up the Ark of the Covenant of Hashem from the house of Oved Edom were joyful.
Since Elokim helped the Leviyim who were carrying the Ark of the Covenant of Hashem, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.

Now David and all the Leviyim who were carrying the Ark, and the singers and Knanyahu, officer of song of the singers, aMeaning of Heb. uncertain.were wrapped-a in robes of fine linen, and David wore a linen ephod.
All Yisrael brought up the Ark of the Covenant of Hashem with shouts and with blasts of the horn, with trumpets and cymbals, playing on harps and lyres.
As the Ark of the Covenant of Hashem arrived at the City of David, Michal daughter of Shaul looked out of the window and saw King David leaping and dancing, and she despised him for it.

aWith vv. 1–3, cf. Shmuel II 6.17–19.They brought in the Ark of Elokim and set it up inside the tent that David had pitched for it, and they sacrificed burnt offerings and offerings of well-being before Elokim.
When David finished sacrificing the burnt offerings and the offerings of well-being, he blessed the people in the name of Hashem.
And he distributed to every person in Yisrael—man and woman alike—to each a loaf of bread, bMeaning of Heb. uncertain.a cake made in a pan, and a raisin cake.-b
He appointed Leviyim to minister before the Ark of Hashem, to invoke, to praise, and to extol Hashem Elokim of Yisrael:
Asaf the chief, Zecharyah second in rank, Yeiel, Shmiramot, Yechiel, Matityahu, Eliav, Bnayahu, Oved Edom, and Yeiel, with harps and lyres, and Asaf sounding the cymbals,
