and Bnayahu and Yachaziel the priests, with trumpets, regularly before the Ark of the Covenant of Elokim.
Then, on that day, David first commissioned Asaf and his kinsmen to give praise to Hashem:

cWith vv. 8–22, cf. Tehillim 105.1–15.“Praise Hashem;
call on His name;
proclaim His deeds among the peoples.

Sing praises unto Him;
speak of all His wondrous acts.

Exult in His holy name;
let all who seek Hashem rejoice.

Turn to Hashem, to His might;dI.e., the Ark; cf. Pss. 78.61; 132.8.
seek His presence constantly.

Remember the wonders He has done;
His portents and the judgments He has pronounced,

O offspring of Yisrael, His servant,
O descendants of Yaakov, His chosen ones.

He is Hashem our Elokim;
His judgments are throughout the earth.

Be ever mindful of His covenant,
the promise He gave for a thousand generations,

that He made with Avraham,
swore to Yitzchak,

and confirmed in a decree for Yaakov,
for Yisrael, as an eternal covenant,

saying, ‘To you I will give the land of Kenaan
as your allotted heritage.’

You were then few in number,
a handful, merely sojourning there,

wandering from nation to nation,
from one kingdom to another.

He allowed no one to oppress them;
He reproved kings on their account,

‘Do not touch My anointed ones;
do not harm My prophets.’

eWith vv. 23–33, cf. Tehillim 96.1–13.“Sing to Hashem, all the earth.
proclaim His victory day after day.

Tell of His glory among the nations,
His wondrous deeds among all peoples.

For Hashem is great and much acclaimed,
He is held in awe by all divine beings.

All the gods of the peoples are mere idols,
but Hashem made the heavens.

Glory and majesty are before Him;
strength and joy are in His place.

“Ascribe to Hashem, O families of the peoples,
ascribe to Hashem glory and strength.

Ascribe to Hashem the glory of His name,
bring tribute and enter before Him,
bow down to Hashem majestic in holiness.

Tremble in His presence, all the earth!
The world stands firm; it cannot be shaken.

Let the heavens rejoice and the earth exult;
let them declare among the nations, “Hashem is King!”

Let the sea and all within it thunder,
the fields and everything in them exult;

then shall all the trees of the forest shout for joy
at the presence of Hashem,
for He is coming to rule the earth.

Praise Hashem for He is good;
His steadfast love is eternal.

fCf. Tehillim 106.47–48.Declare:
Deliver us, O Elokim, our deliverer,
and gather us and save us from the nations,
to acclaim Your holy name,
to glory in Your praise.
Blessed is Hashem, Elokim of Yisrael, from eternity to eternity.” And all the people said, “Amen” and “Praise Hashem.”<sup class="endFootnote">-f</sup>
He left Asaf and his kinsmen there before the Ark of the Covenant of Hashem to minister before the Ark regularly as each day required,
as well as Oved Edom with their kinsmen—68; also Oved Edom son of Yeditun and Chosah as gatekeepers;
also Tzadok the priest and his fellow priests before the Tabernacle of Hashem at the shrine which was in Givon;

to sacrifice burnt offerings to Hashem on the altar of the burnt offering regularly, morning and evening, in accordance with what was prescribed in the Teaching of Hashem with which He charged Yisrael.
With them were Heiman and Yedutun and the other selected men designated by name to give praise to Hashem, “For His steadfast love is eternal.”
Heiman and Yedutun had with them trumpets and cymbals to sound, and instruments for the songs of Elokim; and the sons of Yedutun were to be at the gate.
Then all the people went every one to his home, and David returned to greet his household.

aWith this chapter, cf. Shmuel II 7.When David settled in his palace, David said to the prophet Natan, “Here I am dwelling in a house of cedar, while the Ark of the Covenant of Hashem is under tent-cloths.”
Natan said to David, “Do whatever you have in mind, for Elokim is with you.”
But that same night the word of Elokim came to Natan:
“Go and say to My servant David: Thus said Hashem: You are not the one to build a house for Me to dwell in.
From the day that I brought out Yisrael to this day, I have not dwelt in a house, but have [gone] from tent to tent and from one Tabernacle [to another].
As I moved about wherever Yisrael went, did I ever reproach any of the judges of Yisrael whom I appointed to care for My people Yisrael: Why have you not built Me a house of cedar?
“Further, say thus to My servant David: Thus said Hashem of Hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be ruler of My people Yisrael,
and I have been with you wherever you went, and have cut down all your enemies before you. Moreover, I will give you renown like that of the greatest men on earth.
I will establish a home for My people Yisrael and will plant them firm, so that they shall dwell secure and shall tremble no more. Evil men shall not wear them down anymore as in the past,

ever since I appointed judges over My people Yisrael. I will subdue all your enemies.
And I declare to you: Hashem will build a housebI.e., a dynasty; play on “house” (i.e., Temple) in v. 4. for you.
When your days are done and you follow your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you, one of your own sons, and I will establish his kingship.
He shall build a house for Me, and I will establish his throne forever.
I will be a father to him, and he shall be a son to Me, but I will never withdraw My favor from him as I withdrew it from your predecessor.
I will install him in My house and in My kingship forever, and his throne shall be established forever.”
Natan spoke to David in accordance with all these words and all this prophecy.
Then King David came and sat before Hashem, and he said, “What am I, O Hashem Elokim, and what is my family, that You have brought me thus far?
Yet even this, O Elokim, has seemed too little to You; for You have spoken of Your servant’s house for the future. cMeaning of Heb. uncertain.You regard me as a man of distinction,-c O Hashem Elokim.
What more can David add regarding the honoring of Your servant? You know Your servant.
O Hashem, cMeaning of Heb. uncertain.for Your servant’s sake, and of Your own accord,-c You have wrought this great thing, and made known all these great things.
O Hashem, there is none like You, and there is no other Elokim but You, as we have always heard.

And who is like Your people Yisrael, a unique nation on earth, whom Elokim went and redeemed as His people, winning renown for Yourself for great and marvelous deeds, driving out nations before Your people whom You redeemed from Mitzrayim.
You have established Your people Yisrael as Your very own people forever; and You, O Hashem, have become their Elokim.
“And now, O Hashem, let Your promise concerning Your servant and his house be fulfilled forever; and do as You have promised.

Let it be fulfilled that Your name be glorified forever, in that men will say,‘Hashem of Hosts, Elokim of Yisrael, is Yisrael’s Elokim’; and may the house of Your servant David be established before You.
Because You, my Elokim, have revealed to Your servant that You will build a house for him, Your servant has ventured to pray to You.
And now, O Hashem, You are Elokim and You have made this gracious promise to Your servant.
Now, it has pleased You to bless Your servant’s house, that it abide before You forever; for You, O Hashem, have blessed and are blessed forever.”
aWith this chapter, cf. Shmuel II 8.Sometime afterward, David attacked the Plishtim and subdued them; and David took Gat and its dependencies from the Plishtim.
He also defeated the Moavim; the Moavim became tributary vassals of David.
David defeated Hadadezer, king of Tzova Chamat, who was on his way to set up his monument at the Perat River.
David captured 1,000 chariots and 7,000 horsemen and 20,000 foot soldiers of his force; and David hamstrung all the chariot horses except for 100, which he retained.
And when the Aram of Damesek came to the aid of King Hadadezer of Tzova Chamat, David struck down 22,000 of the Aram.
David stationed [garrisons] in Aram of Damesek, and the Aram became tributary vassals of David. Hashem gave David victory wherever he went.
David took the gold shieldsbOr “quivers.” carried by Hadadezer’s retinue and brought them to Yerushalayim;
and from Tivchat and Kun, towns of Hadadezer, David took a vast amount of copper, from which Shlomo made the bronze tank, the columns, and the bronze vessels.
When King Tou of Chamat heard that David had defeated the entire army of King Hadadezer of Tzova,

he sent his son Hadoram to King David to greet him and to congratulate him on his military victory over Hadadezer—for Hadadezer had been at war with Tou; [he brought with him] all manner of gold, silver, and copper objects.
King David dedicated these to Hashem, along with the other silver and gold that he had taken from all the nations: from Edom, Moav, and Amon; from the Plishtim and the Amaleki.
Abshai son of Tzruyah struck down Edom in the Valley of Salt, 18,000 in all.
He stationed garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomim became vassals of David. Hashem gave David victory wherever he went.
David reigned over all Yisrael, and David executed true justice among all his people.
Yoav son of Tzruyah was commander of the army; Yehoshafat son of Achilud was recorder;
Tzadok son of Achituv and Avimelech son of Evyatar were priests; Shavsha was scribe;
Bnayahu son of Yehoyada was commander of the Kreti and the Pleti; and David’s sons were first ministers of the king.
aWith this chapter, cf. Shmuel II 10.Sometime afterward, Nachash the king of Bnei Amon died, and his son succeeded him as king.

David said, “I will keep faith with Chanun son of Nachash, since his father kept faith with me.” David sent messengers with condolences to him over his father. But when David’s courtiers came to the land of Amon to Chanun, with condolences,

the Amoni officials said to Chanun, “Do you think David is really honoring your father just because he sent you men with condolences? Why, it is to explore, to subvert, and to spy out the land that his courtiers have come to you.”
So Chanun seized David’s courtiers, shaved them, and cut away half of their garments up to the buttocks, and sent them off.

When David was told about the men, he dispatched others to meet them, for the men were greatly embarrassed. And the king gave orders, “Stay in Yericho until your beards grow back; then you can return.”
Bnei Amon realized that they had incurred the wrath of David; so Chanun and Bnei Amon sent 1,000 silver talents to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram Naharayim, Aram Ma'achah, and Tzova.
They hired 32,000 chariots, the king of Ma'achah, and his army, who came and encamped before Meidva. Bnei Amon were mobilized from their cities and came to do battle.
On learning this, David sent out Yoav and the whole army, [including] the professional fighters.
Bnei Amon marched out and took up their battle position at the entrance of the city, while the kings who came [took their stand] separately in the open.
Yoav saw that there was a battle line against him both front and rear. So he made a selection from all the picked men of Yisrael and arrayed them against the Aram,
and the rest of the troops he put under the command of his brother Avishai and arrayed them against Bnei Amon.
Yoav said, “If the Aram prove too strong for me, you come to my aid; and if Bnei Amon prove too strong for you, I will come to your aid.
Let us be strong and resolute for the sake of our people and the towns of our Elokim; and Hashem will do what He deems right.”
Yoav and the troops with him marched into battle against the Aram, who fled before him.
And when Bnei Amon saw that the Aram had fled, they too fled before his brother Avishai, and withdrew into the city. So Yoav went to Yerushalayim.
When the Aram saw that they had been routed by Yisrael, they sent messengers to bring out the Aram from across the Perat; Shofach, Hadadezer’s army commander, led them.
David was informed of it; he assembled all Yisrael, crossed the Yarden, and came and took up positions against them. David drew up his forces against Aram; and they fought with him.
But the Aram were put to flight by Yisrael. David killed 7,000 Arami charioteers and 40,000 footmen; he also killed Shofach, the army commander.
And when all the vassals of Hadadezer saw that they had been routed by Yisrael, they submitted to David and became his vassals. And the Aram would not help Bnei Amon anymore.

aWith vv. 1–3, cf. Shmuel II 11.1; 12.30–31.At the turn of the year, the season when kings go out [to battle], Yoav led out the army force and devastated the land of Amon, and then besieged Rabah, while David remained in Yerushalayim; Yoav reduced Rabah and left it in ruins.

David took the crown from the head of their king; he found that it weighed a talent of gold, and in it were precious stones. It was placed on David’s head. He also carried off a vast amount of booty from the city.

He led out the people who lived there and bMeaning of Heb. uncertain. Shmuel II 12.31 has “set them to work.”he hacked them-b with saws and iron threshing boards and axes;cHeb. megeroth; cf. Shmuel II 12.31 magzeroth, “axes.” David did thus to all the towns of Amon. Then David and all the troops returned to Yerushalayim.
After this, fighting broke out with the Plishtim at Gezer; that was when Sibchai the Chushati killed Sipai, a descendant of the Refaim, and they were humbled.
Again there was fighting with the Plishtim, and Elchanan son of Yair killed Lachmi, the brother of Golyat the Giti; his spear had a shaft like a weaver’s beam.
Once again there was fighting at Gat. There was a giant of a man who had twenty-four fingers [and toes], six [on each hand] and six [on each foot]; he too was descended from the Rafah.
When he taunted Yisrael, Yehonatan son of David’s brother Shima killed him.
These were descended from the Rafah in Gat, and they fell by the hands of David and his men.
aWith vv. 1–26, cf. Shmuel II 24.Satan arose against Yisrael and incited David to number Yisrael.
David said to Yoav and to the commanders of the army, “Go and count Yisrael from Beer Sheva to Dan and bring me information as to their number.”
Yoav answered, “May Hashem increase His people a hundredfold; my lord king, are they not all subjects of my lord? Why should my lord require this? Why should it be a cause of guilt for Yisrael?”
However, the king’s command to Yoav remained firm, so Yoav set out and traversed all Yisrael; he then came to Yerushalayim.
Yoav reported to David the number of the people that had been recorded. All Yisrael comprised 1,100,000 ready to draw the sword, while in Yehudah there were 470,000 men ready to draw the sword.
He did not record among them Levi and Binyamin, because the king’s command had become repugnant to Yoav.
Elokim was displeased about this matter and He struck Yisrael.
David said to Elokim, “I have sinned grievously in having done this thing; please remit the guilt of Your servant, for I have acted foolishly.”
Hashem ordered Gad, David’s seer:
“Go and tell David: Thus said Hashem: I offer you three things; choose one of them and I will bring it upon you.”
Gad came to David and told him, “Thus said Hashem: Select for yourself

a three-year famine; or that you be swept away three months before your adversaries with the sword of your enemies overtaking you; or three days of the sword of Hashem, pestilence in the land, the angel of Hashem wreaking destruction throughout the territory of Yisrael. Now consider what reply I shall take back to Him who sent me.”
David said to Gad, “I am in great distress. Let me fall into the hands of Hashem, for His compassion is very great; and let me not fall into the hands of men.”
Hashem sent a pestilence upon Yisrael, and 70,000 men fell in Yisrael.

Elokim sent an angel to Yerushalayim to destroy it, but as he was about to wreak destruction, Hashem saw and renounced further punishment and said to the destroying angel, “Enough! Stay your hand!” The angel of Hashem was then standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Yevusi.

David looked up and saw the angel of Hashem standing between heaven and earth, with a drawn sword in his hand directed against Yerushalayim. David and the elders, covered in sackcloth, threw themselves on their faces.

David said to Elokim, “Was it not I alone who ordered the numbering of the people? I alone am guilty, and have caused severe harm; but these sheep, what have they done? O Hashem my Elokim, let Your hand fall upon me and my father’s house, and let not Your people be plagued!”
The angel of Hashem told Gad to inform David that David should go and set up an altar to Hashem on the threshing floor of Ornan the Yevusi.
David went up, following Gad’s instructions, which he had delivered in the name of Hashem.
Ornan too saw the angel; his four sons who were with him hid themselves while Ornan kept on threshing wheat.
David came to Ornan; when Ornan looked up, he saw David and came off the threshing floor and bowed low to David, with his face to the ground.
David said to Ornan, “Sell me the site of the threshing floor, that I may build on it an altar to Hashem. Sell it to me at the full price, that the plague against the people will be checked.”

Ornan said to David, “Take it and let my lord the king do whatever he sees fit. See, I donate oxen for burnt offerings, and the threshing boards for wood, as well as wheat for a meal offering—I donate all of it.”
But King David replied to Ornan, “No, I will buy them at the full price. I cannot make a present to Hashem of what belongs to you, or sacrifice a burnt offering that has cost me nothing.”
So David paid Ornan for the site 600 shekels’ worth of gold.
And David built there an altar to Hashem and sacrificed burnt offerings and offerings of well-being. He invoked Hashem, who answered him with fire from heaven on the altar of burnt offerings.
Hashem ordered the angel to return his sword to its sheath.
At that time, when David saw that Hashem answered him at the threshing floor of Ornan the Yevusi, then he sacrificed there—
for the Tabernacle of Hashem, which Moshe had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offerings, were at that time in the shrine at Givon,
and David was unable to go to it to worship Elokim because he was terrified by the sword of the angel of Hashem.
David said, “Here will be the House of Hashem and here the altar of burnt offerings for Yisrael.”
David gave orders to assemble the aliens living in the land of Yisrael, and assigned them to be hewers, to quarry and dress stones for building the House of Elokim.
Much iron for nails for the doors of the gates and for clasps did David lay aside, and so much copper it could not be weighed,
and cedar logs without number—for the Tzidonim and the Tzorim brought many cedar logs to David.

For David thought, “My son Shlomo is an untried youth, and the House to be built for Hashem is to be made exceedingly great to win fame and glory throughout all the lands; let me then lay aside material for him.” So David laid aside much material before he died.
Then he summoned his son Shlomo and charged him with building the House for Hashem Elokim of Yisrael.
David said to Shlomo, “My son, I wanted to build a House for the name of Hashem my Elokim.
But the word of Hashem came to me, saying,‘You have shed much blood and fought great battles; you shall not build a House for My name, for you have shed much blood on the earth in My sight.

But you will have a son who will be a man at rest, for I will give him rest from all his enemies on all sides; ShlomoaHeb. Shelomoh. will be his name and I shall confer peacebHeb. shalom. and quiet on Yisrael in his time.
He will build a House for My name; he shall be a son to Me and I to him a father, and I will establish his throne of kingship over Yisrael forever.’
Now, my son, may Hashem be with you, and may you succeed in building the House of Hashem your Elokim as He promised you would.
Only let God give you sense and understanding and put you in charge of Yisrael and the observance of the Teaching of Hashem your God.
Then you shall succeed, if you observantly carry out the laws and the rules that Hashem charged Moshe to lay upon Yisrael. Be strong and of good courage; do not be afraid or dismayed.

See, cWith Targum; or “in my poverty.”by denying myself,-c I have laid aside for the House of Hashem one hundred thousand talents of gold and one million talents of silver, and so much copper and iron it cannot be weighed; I have also laid aside wood and stone, and you shall add to them.
An abundance of workmen is at your disposal—hewers, workers in stone and wood, and every kind of craftsman in every kind of material—
gold, silver, copper, and iron without limit. Go and do it, and may Hashem be with you.”
David charged all the officers of Yisrael to support his son Shlomo,

“See, Hashem your Elokim is with you, and He will give you rest on every side, for He delivered the inhabitants of the land into my hand so that the land lies conquered before Hashem and before His people.

Now, set your minds and hearts on worshiping Hashem your Elokim, and go build the Sanctuary of Hashem your Elokim so that you may bring the Ark of the Covenant of Hashem and the holy vessels of Elokim to the house that is built for the name of Hashem.”
When David reached a ripe old age, he made his son Shlomo king over Yisrael.
Then David assembled all the officers of Yisrael and the priests and the Leviyim.
The Leviyim, from the age of thirty and upward, were counted; the head-count of their males was 38,000:
of these there were 24,000 in charge of the work of the House of Hashem, 6,000 officers and magistrates,
4,000 gatekeepers, and 4,000 for praising Hashem “with instruments I devised for singing praises.”

David formed them into divisions:
The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kehat, and Merari.
The Gershuni: Ladan and Shimi.
The sons of Ladan: Yechiel the chief, Zetam, and Yoel—3.
The sons of Shimi: Shlomit, Chaziel, and Haran—3. These were the chiefs of the clans of the Ladanites.
And the sons of Shimi: Yachat, Zina, Yeush, and Briah; these were the sons of Shimi—4.
Yachat was the chief and Zizah the second, but Yeush and Briah did not have many children, so they were enrolled together as a single clan.
The sons of Kehat: Amram, Yitzhar, Chevron, and Uziel—4.

The sons of Amram: Aharon and Moshe. Aharon was set apart, he and his sons, forever, to be consecrated as most holy, to make burnt offerings to Hashem and serve Him and pronounce blessings in His name forever.
As for Moshe, the man of Elokim, his sons were named after the tribe of Levi.
The sons of Moshe: Gershom and Eliezer.
The sons of Gershom: Shvuel the chief.
And the sons of Eliezer were: Rechavyahu the chief. Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rechavyahu were very numerous.
The sons of Yitzhar: Shlomit the chief.
The sons of Chevron: Yeriyahu the chief, Amaryah the second, Yachaziel the third, and Yekamam the fourth.
The sons of Uziel: Michah the chief and Yishiyah the second.
The sons of Merari: Machli and Mushi. The sons of Machli: Elazar and Kish.
Elazar died having no sons but only daughters; the sons of Kish, their kinsmen, married them.
The sons of Mushi: Machli, Eder, and Yeremot—3.

These are the sons of Levi by clans, with their clan chiefs as they were enrolled, with a list of their names by heads, who did the work of the service of the House of Hashem from the age of twenty and upward.
For David said, “Hashem Elokim of Yisrael has given rest to His people and made His dwelling in Yerushalayim forever.
Therefore the Leviyim need not carry the Tabernacle and all its various service vessels.”
Among the last acts of David was the counting of the Leviyim from the age of twenty and upward.

For their appointment was alongside Bnei Aharon for the service of the House of Hashem, to look after the courts and the chambers, and the purity of all the holy things, and the performance of the service of the House of Elokim,
and the rows of bread, and the fine flour for the meal offering, and the unleavened wafers, and the cakes made on the griddle and soaked, and every measure of capacity and length;
and to be present every morning to praise and extol Hashem, and at evening too,
and whenever offerings were made to Hashem, according to the quantities prescribed for them, on sabbaths, new moons and holidays, regularly, before Hashem;
and so to keep watch over the Tent of Meeting, over the holy things, and over Bnei Aharon their kinsmen, for the service of the House of Hashem.

The divisions of Bnei Aharon were:
The sons of Aharon: Nadav and Avihu, Elazar and Itamar.
Nadav and Avihu died in the lifetime of their father, and they had no children, so Elazar and Itamar served as priests.
David, Tzadok of the sons of Elazar, and Achimelech of the sons of Itamar divided them into offices by their tasks.
The sons of Elazar turned out to be more numerous by male heads than the sons of Itamar, so they divided the sons of Elazar into sixteen chiefs of clans and the sons of Itamar into eight clans.
They divided them by lot, both on an equal footing, since they were all sanctuary officers and officers of Elokim—the sons of Elazar and the sons of Itamar.

Shmayah son of Nathanel, the scribe, who was of the Leviyim, registered them under the eye of the king, the officers, and Tzadok the priest, and Achimelech son of Evyatar, and the chiefs of clans of the priests and Leviyim—aMeaning of Heb. uncertain.one clan more taken for Elazar for each one taken of Itamar.-a
The first lot fell on Yehoyariv; the second on Yedayah;
the third on Charim; the fourth on Seorim;
the fifth on Malkiyah; the sixth on Miyamin;
the seventh on Hakotz; the eighth on Aviyah;
the ninth on Yeshua; the tenth on Shchanyah;
the eleventh on Elyashiv; the twelfth on Yakim;
the thirteenth on Chupah; the fourteenth on Yeshevav;
the fifteenth on Bilgah; the sixteenth on Imer;
the seventeenth on Chezir; the eighteenth on Hapitzetz;
the nineteenth on Petachyah; the twentieth on Yechezkel;
the twenty-first on Yachin; the twenty-second on Gamul;
the twenty-third on Dlayah; the twenty-fourth on Ma'azyahu.
According to this allocation of offices by tasks, they were to enter the House of Hashem as was laid down for them by Aharon their father, as Hashem Elokim of Yisrael had commanded him.
The remaining Leviyim: the sons of Amram: Shvuel; the sons of Shvuel: Jehdeiah;
Rechavyahu. The sons of Rechavyahu: Yishiyah, the chief.
Yitzhari: Shlomot. The sons of Shlomot: Yachat
and Bnai, Yeriyahu; the second, Amaryah; the third, Yachaziel; the fourth, Yekamam.
The sons of Uziel: Michah. The sons of Michah: Shamir.
The brother of Michah: Yishiyah. The sons of Yishiyah: Zecharyah.
The sons of Merari: Machli and Mushi. The sons of Ya'aziyahu, his son—
the sons of Merari by Ya'aziyahu his son: Shoham, Zakur, and Ivri.
Machli: Elazar; he had no sons.
Kish: the sons of Kish: Yerachme'el.
The sons of Mushi: Machli, Eder, and Yerimot. These were the sons of the Leviyim by their clans.

These too cast lots corresponding to their kinsmen, the sons of Aharon, under the eye of King David and Tzadok and Achimelech and the chiefs of the clans of the priests and Leviyim, on the principle of “chief and youngest brother alike.”

David and the officers of the army set apart for service the sons of Asaf, of Heiman, and of Yedutun, who prophesied to the accompaniment of lyres, harps, and cymbals. The list of men who performed this work, according to their service, was:
Sons of Asaf: Zakur, Yosef, Netanyah, and Asarelah—sons of Asaf under the charge of Asaf, who prophesied by order of the king.
Yedutun—the sons of Yedutun: Gedalyahu, Tzri, Yeshayah, Chashavyah, Matityahu—6, under the charge of their father Yedutun, who, accompanied on the harp, prophesied, praising and extolling Hashem.
Heiman—the sons of Heiman: Bukiyahu, Matanyah, Uziel, Shvuel, Yerimot, Chananyah, Chanani, Eliatah, Gidalti, Romamti Ezer, Yoshbekashah, Maloti, Hotir, and Machaziot;
all these were sons of Heiman, the seer of the king, [who uttered] prophecies of Elokim for His greater glory. Elokim gave Heiman fourteen sons and three daughters;

all these were under the charge of their father for the singing in the House of Hashem, to the accompaniment of cymbals, harps, and lyres, for the service of the House of Elokim by order of the king. Asaf, Yedutun, and Heiman—
their total number with their kinsmen, trained singers of Hashem—all the masters, 288.
They cast lots for shifts on the principle of “small and great alike, like master like apprentice.”
The first lot fell to Asaf—to Yosef; the second, to Gedalyahu, he and his brothers and his sons—12;
the third, to Zakur: his sons and his brothers—12;
the fourth, to Izri: his sons and his brothers—12;
the fifth, to Netanyah: his sons and his brothers—12;
the sixth, to Bukiyahu: his sons and his brothers—12;
the seventh, to Yesarelah: his sons and his brothers—12;
the eighth, to Yeshayah: his sons and his brothers—12;
the ninth, to Matanyah: his sons and his brothers—12;
the tenth, to Shimi: his sons and his brothers—12;
the eleventh to Azarel: his sons and his brothers—12;
the twelfth, to Chashavyah: his sons and his brothers—12;
the thirteenth, to Shvuel: his sons and his brothers—12;
the fourteenth, to Matityahu: his sons and his brothers—12;
the fifteenth, to Yeremot: his sons and his brothers—12;
the sixteenth, to Chananyah: his sons and his brothers—12;
the seventeenth, to Yoshbekashah: his sons and his brothers—12;
the eighteenth, to Chanani: his sons and his brothers—12;
the nineteenth, to Maloti: his sons and his brothers—12;
the twentieth, to Eliatah: his sons and his brothers—12;
the twenty-first, to Hotir: his sons and his brothers—12;
the twenty-second, to Gidalti: his sons and his brothers—12;
the twenty-third, to Machaziot: his sons and his brothers—12;
the twenty-fourth, to Romamti Ezer: his sons and his brothers—12.
The divisions of the gatekeepers: Bnei Korach: Meshelemyah son of Kore, of the sons of Asaf.
Sons of Meshelemyah: Zecharyah the firstborn, Yediael the second, Zvadyah the third, Yatniel the fourth,
Eilam the fifth, Yehochanan the sixth, Elyehoeinai the seventh.
Sons of Oved Edom: Shmayah the first-born, Yehozavad the second, Yoach the third, Sachar the fourth, Netanel the fifth,
Amiel the sixth, Yissachar the seventh, Peuletai the eighth—for Elokim had blessed him.
To his son Shmayah were born sons who exercised authority in their clans because they were men of substance.
The sons of Shmayah: Othni, Rephael, Oved, Elzavad—his brothers, men of ability, were Elihu and Smachyahu.
All these, sons of Oved Edom; they and their sons and brothers, strong and able men for the service—62 of Oved Edom.
Meshelemyah had sons and brothers, able men—18.
Chosah of Bnei Merari had sons: Shimri the chief (he was not the first-born, but his father designated him chief),
Chilkiyahu the second, Tvalyahu the third, Zecharyah the fourth. All the sons and brothers of Chosah—13.
These are the divisions of the gatekeepers, by their chief men, [who worked in] shifts corresponding to their kinsmen, ministering in the House of Hashem.
They cast lots, small and great alike, by clans, for each gate.
The lot for the east [gate] fell to Shelemyahu. Then they cast lots [for] Zecharyah his son, a prudent counselor, and his lot came out to be the north [gate].
For Oved Edom, the south [gate], and for his sons, the vestibule.
For Shupim and for Chosah, the west [gate], with the Shalechet gate on the ascending highway. Watch corresponded to watch:
At the east—six Leviyim; at the north—four daily; at the south—four daily; at the vestibule—two by two;
at the colonnade on the west—four at the causeway and two at the colonnade.
These were the divisions of the gatekeepers of the sons of Korach and the sons of Merari.
And the Leviyim: Achiyah over the treasuries of the House of Elokim and the treasuries of the dedicated things.
The sons of Ladan: the sons of the Gershuni belonging to Ladan; the chiefs of the clans of Ladan, the Gershuni—Yechieli.
The sons of Yechieli: Zetam and Yoel; his brother was over the treasuries of the House of Hashem.
Of the Amrami, the Yitzhari, the Chevroni, the Ozieli:
Shvuel son of Gershom son of Moshe was the chief officer over the treasuries.
And his brothers: Eliezer, his son Rechavyahu, his son Yeshayah, his son Yoram, his son Zichri, his son Shlomit—

that Shlomit and his brothers were over all the treasuries of dedicated things that were dedicated by King David and the chiefs of the clans, and the officers of thousands and hundreds and the other army officers;
they dedicated some of the booty of the wars to maintain the House of Hashem.
All that Shmuel the seer had dedicated, and Shaul son of Kish, and Avner son of Ner, and Yoav son of Tzruyah—or [what] any other man had dedicated, was under the charge of Shlomit and his brothers.
The Yitzhari: Knanyahu and his sons were over Yisrael as clerks and magistrates for affairs outside [the sanctuary].
The Chevroni: Chashavyah and his brothers, capable men, 1,700, supervising Yisrael on the west side of the Yarden in all matters of Hashem and the service of the king.
The Chevroni: Yeriyahu, the chief of the Chevroni—they were investigated in the fortieth year of David’s reign by clans of all their lines, and men of substance were found among them in Yazer Gilad.
His brothers, able men, 2,700, chiefs of clans—David put them in charge of the Reuveni, the Gadi, and the half-tribe of Menashe in all matters of Elokim and matters of the king.

The number of Bnei Yisrael—chiefs of clans, officers of thousands and hundreds and their clerks, who served the king in all matters of the divisions, who worked in monthly shifts during all the months of the year—each division, 24,000.
Over the first division for the first month—Yashovam son of Zavdiel; his division had 24,000.
Of the sons of Peretz, he, the chief of all the officers of the army, [served] for the first month.
Over the division of the second month—Dodai the Achochi; Miklot was chief officer of his division; his division had 24,000.
The third army officer for the third month—Bnayahu son of Yehoyada, the chief priest; his division had 24,000.
That was Bnayahu, one of the warriors of the thirty and over the thirty; and [over] his division was Amizavad his son.
The fourth, for the fourth month, Asahel brother of Yoav, and his son Zvadyah after him; his division had 24,000.
The fifth, for the fifth month, the officer Shamhut the Izrahite; his division had 24,000.
The sixth, for the sixth month, Ira son of Ikesh the Tekoi; his division had 24,000.
The seventh, for the seventh month, Cheletz the Ploni, of Bnei Efraim; his division had 24,000.
The eighth, for the eighth month, Sibchai the Chushati, of Zerach; his division had 24,000.
The ninth, for the ninth month, Aviezer the Anatoti, of Binyamin; his division had 24,000.
The tenth, for the tenth month, Mahrai the Netofati, of Zerach; his division had 24,000.
The eleventh, for the eleventh month, Bnayahu the Piratoni, of Bnei Efraim; his division had 24,000.
The twelfth, for the twelfth month, Cheldai the Netofati, of Otniel; his division had 24,000.
Over the tribes of Yisrael: Reuven: the chief officer, Eliezer son of Zichri. Shimon: Shfatyah son of Maaca.
Levi: Chashavyah son of Kmuel. Aharon: Tzadok.
Yehudah: Elihu, of the brothers of David. Yissachar: Omri son of Michael.
Zevulun: Ishmaiah son of Ovadyah. Naftali: Yerimot son of Azriel.
Bnei Efraim: Hoshea son of Azazyahu. The half-tribe of Menashe: Yoel son of Pedayah.
Half Menashe in Gilad: Ido son of Zecharyah. Binyamin: Jaasiel son of Avner.
Dan: Azarel son of Yerocham. These were the officers of the tribes of Yisrael.
David did not take a census of those under twenty years of age, for Hashem had promised to make Yisrael as numerous as the stars of heaven.
Yoav son of Tzruyah did begin to count them, but he did not finish; wrath struck Yisrael on account of this, and the census was not entered into the account of the chronicles of King David.
Over the royal treasuries: Azmavet son of Adiel. Over the treasuries in the country—in the towns, the hamlets, and the citadels: Yehonatan son of Uziyahu.
Over the field laborers in agricultural work: Ezri son of Kluv.
Over the vineyards: Shimi the Ramati. And over the produce in the vineyards for wine cellars: Zavdi the Shifmi.
Over the olive trees and the sycamores in the Shfelah: Ba'al Chanan the Gederite. Over the oil-stores: Yoash.
Over the cattle pasturing in Sharon: Shirtai the Sharoni. And over the cattle in the valleys: Shafat son of Adlai.
Over the camels: Obil the Yishmeeli. And over the she-asses: Jehdeiah the Meronoti.
Over the flocks: Jaziz the Hagri. All these were stewards of the property of King David.
Yehonatan, David’s uncle, was a counselor, a master, and a scribe: Yechiel son of Chachmoni was with the king’s sons.
Ahitophel was a counselor to the king. Chushai the Arki was the king’s friend.
After Ahitophel were Yehoyada son of Bnayahu and Evyatar. The commander of the king’s army was Yoav.

David assembled all the officers of Yisrael—the tribal officers, the divisional officers who served the king, the captains of thousands and the captains of hundreds, and the stewards of all the property and cattle of the king and his sons, with the eunuchs and the warriors, all the men of substance—to Yerushalayim.

King David rose to his feet and said, “Hear me, my brothers, my people! I wanted to build a resting-place for the Ark of the Covenant of Hashem, for the footstool of our Elokim, and I laid aside material for building.
But Elokim said to me,‘You will not build a house for My name, for you are a man of battles and have shed blood.’

Hashem Elokim of Yisrael chose me of all my father’s house to be king over Yisrael forever. For He chose Yehudah to be ruler, and of the family of Yehudah, my father’s house; and of my father’s sons, He preferred to make me king over all Yisrael;
and of all my sons—for many are the sons Hashem gave me—He chose my son Shlomo to sit on the throne of the kingdom of Hashem over Yisrael.
He said to me,‘It will be your son Shlomo who will build My House and My courts, for I have chosen him to be a son to Me, and I will be a father to him.
I will establish his kingdom forever, if he keeps firmly to the observance of My commandments and rules as he does now.’

And now, in the sight of all Yisrael, the congregation of Hashem, and in the hearing of our Elokim, [I say:] Observe and apply yourselves to all the commandments of Hashem your Elokim in order that you may possess this good land and bequeath it to your children after you forever.

“And you, my son Shlomo, know the Elokim of your father, and serve Him with single mind and fervent heart, for Hashem searches all minds and discerns the design of every thought; if you seek Him He will be available to you, but if you forsake Him He will abandon you forever.
See then, Hashem chose you to build a house as the sanctuary; be strong and do it.”
David gave his son Shlomo the plan of the porch and its houses, its storerooms and its upper chambers and inner chambers; and of the place of the Ark-cover;

and the plan of all that he had by the spirit: of the courts of the House of Hashem and all its surrounding chambers, and of the treasuries of the House of Elokim and of the treasuries of the holy things;
the divisions of priests and Leviyim for all the work of the service of the House of Hashem and all the vessels of the service of the House of Hashem;
and gold, the weight of gold for vessels of every sort of use; silver for all the vessels of silver by weight, for all the vessels of every kind of service;
the weight of the gold lampstands and their gold lamps, and the weight of the silver lampstands, each lampstand and its silver lamps, according to the use of every lampstand;
and the weight of gold for the tables of the rows of bread, for each table, and of silver for the silver tables;
and of the pure gold for the forks and the basins and the jars; and the weight of the gold bowls, every bowl; and the weight of the silver bowls, each and every bowl;
the weight of refined gold for the incense altar and the gold for the figure of the chariot—the cherubim—those with outspread wings screening the Ark of the Covenant of Hashem.
“All this that Hashem made me understand by His hand on me, I give you in writing—the plan of all the works.”

David said to his son Shlomo, “Be strong and of good courage and do it; do not be afraid or dismayed, for Hashem Elokim my Elokim is with you; He will not fail you or forsake you till all the work on the House of Hashem is done.

Here are the divisions of the priests and Leviyim for all kinds of service of the House of Elokim, and with you in all the work are willing men, skilled in all sorts of tasks; also the officers and all the people are at your command.”

King David said to the entire assemblage, “Elokim has chosen my son Shlomo alone, an untried lad, although the work to be done is vast—for the templeaLit. “fortress.” is not for a man but for Hashem Elokim.

I have spared no effort to lay up for the House of my Elokim gold for golden objects, silver for silver, copper for copper, iron for iron, wood for wooden, onyx-stone and inlay-stone, stone of antimony and variegated colors—every kind of precious stone and much marble.
Besides, out of my solicitude for the House of my Elokim, I gave over my private hoard of gold and silver to the House of my Elokim—in addition to all that I laid aside for the holy House:
3,000 gold talents of Ofir gold, and 7,000 talents of refined silver for covering the walls of the houses
(gold for golden objects, silver for silver for all the work)—into the hands of craftsmen. Now who is going to make a freewill offering and devote himself today to Hashem?”
The officers of the clans and the officers of the tribes of Yisrael and the captains of thousands and hundreds and the supervisors of the king’s work made freewill offerings,
giving for the work of the House of Elokim: 5,000 talents of gold, 10,000 darics, 10,000 talents of silver, 18,000 talents of copper, 100,000 talents of iron.
Whoever had stones in his possession gave them to the treasury of the House of Hashem in the charge of Yechiel the Gershuni.
The people rejoiced over the freewill offerings they made, for with a whole heart they made freewill offerings to Hashem; King David also rejoiced very much.
David blessed Hashem in front of all the assemblage; David said, “Blessed are You, Hashem, Elokim of Yisrael our father, from eternity to eternity.
Yours, Hashem, are greatness, might, splendor, triumph, and majesty—yes, all that is in heaven and on earth; to You, Hashem, belong kingship and preeminence above all.
Riches and honor are Yours to dispense; You have dominion over all; with You are strength and might, and it is in Your power to make anyone great and strong.
Now, Elokim, we praise You and extol Your glorious name.
Who am I and who are my people, that we should have the means to make such a freewill offering; but all is from You, and it is Your gift that we have given to You.
For we are sojourners with You, mere transients like our fathers; our days on earth are like a shadow, with nothing in prospect.
O Hashem our Elokim, all this great mass that we have laid aside to build You a House for Your holy name is from You, and it is all Yours.

I know, Elokim, that You search the heart and desire uprightness; I, with upright heart, freely offered all these things; now Your people, who are present here—I saw them joyously making freewill offerings.
O Hashem Elokim of Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yisrael, our fathers, remember this to the eternal credit of the thoughts of Your people’s hearts, and make their hearts constant toward You.

As to my son Shlomo, give him a whole heart to observe Your commandments, Your admonitions, and Your laws, and to fulfill them all, and to build this templeaLit. “fortress.” for which I have made provision.”
David said to the whole assemblage, “Now bless Hashem your Elokim.” All the assemblage blessed Hashem Elokim of their fathers, and bowed their heads low to Hashem and the king.

They offered sacrifices to Hashem and made burnt offerings to Hashem on the morrow of that day: 1,000 bulls, 1,000 rams, 1,000 lambs, with their libations; [they made] sacrifices in great number for all Yisrael,
and they ate and drank in the presence of Hashem on that day with great joy. They again proclaimed Shlomo son of David king, and they anointed him as ruler before Hashem, and Tzadok as high priest.
Shlomo successfully took over the throne of Hashem as king instead of his father David, and all went well with him. All Yisrael accepted him;
all the officials and the warriors, and the sons of King David as well, gave their hand in support of King Shlomo.
Hashem made Shlomo exceedingly great in the eyes of all Yisrael, and endowed him with a regal majesty that no king of Yisrael before him ever had.
Thus David son of Yishai reigned over all Yisrael;
the length of his reign over Yisrael was forty years: he reigned seven years in Chevron and thirty-three years in Yerushalayim.
He died at a ripe old age, having enjoyed long life, riches and honor, and his son Shlomo reigned in his stead.
The acts of King David, early and late, are recorded in the history of Shmuel the seer, the history of Natan the prophet, and the history of Gad the seer,
together with all the mighty deeds of his kingship and the events that befell him and Yisrael and all the kingdoms of the earth.
